title: Multi-Agent Collaboration for Complex Systems Modeling
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to modeling complex systems utilizing the principles of multi-agent collaboration. Traditional methods for complex system modeling often rely on static representations, struggling to capture the inherent dynamism and adaptive behavior observed in real-world scenarios. We propose a framework where complex systems are decomposed into a network of interacting intelligent agents. Each agent is responsible for managing a specific aspect of the system, communicating with others through a defined protocol, and adapting its behavior based on received information. The core of the method leverages reinforcement learning or evolutionary algorithms to optimize the strategies of these agents, allowing the system to learn and respond effectively to changing conditions. This dynamic modeling approach enables real-time control and optimization, offering a significant improvement over static modeling techniques. The effectiveness of the proposed framework is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, outlining a flexible and scalable methodology for tackling complex system challenges.

title: DLGNet: A Deep Learning and Generative Framework for Privacy-preserving PII De-identification with Semantic Verification
abstract: The rapid growth of unstructured textual data in domains such as healthcare, education, and enterprise systems has increased the risk of inadvertent exposure of Personally Identifiable Information (PII).Effective deidentification is essential to enable secure data sharing while preserving privacy and regulatory compliance.Existing approaches, including rule-based and deep learning-based Named Entity Recognition (NER) methods, primarily focus on detection and often lack contextual validation and robust replacement mechanisms, leading to information loss or residual privacy risks.This work proposes DLGNet, a pipeline-based integrated framework PII de-identification framework that integrates DeBERTa-based token-level detection, LLM-based semantic verification, and type-aware replacement.A BIO-tagged DeBERTa model identifies candidate PII spans, which are refined using a TinyLlamabased semantic verification module for contextual validation.Detected entities are then replaced using a hybrid generative and rule-based strategy to ensure irreversible transformation while preserving textual coherence.Experimental results demonstrate strong recall-oriented performance, achieving precision of 90.3%, recall of 94.7%, F1-score of 92.4%, and Fβ-score (β = 5) of 94.52%.Utility evaluation shows a length ratio of 0.96 and token overlap of 0.73, indicating effective preservation of textual structure and semantics.The proposed framework provides a unified and practical solution for privacy-preserving text processing by jointly improving detection accuracy, contextual reliability, and data utility.

title: FabroGym: registration of an explainability requirements analysis for a fitness routine recommendation component
abstract: Estudio de caso sobre requisitos no funcionales de explicabilidad para un componente propuesto de recomendación de rutinas. Antes del registro OSF se realizaron seis walkthroughs generales de FabroGym: tres con participantes técnicos y tres con participantes no técnicos. Estas sesiones constituyen evidencia empírica previa/formativa y no datos confirmatorios preregistrados. No se presupone que una explicación estructurada específica haya sido evaluada en las seis sesiones. Después del registro se realizará la codificación sistemática de la evidencia, se identificarán de forma trazable los fragmentos pertinentes para explicabilidad, se formularán o ajustarán candidatos a RNF y, si aún está pendiente, se realizará el member checking final.

title: AOI-Net: Structural Face AOI-Guided Eye-Gaze Track Representation Learning for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
abstract: Eye-movement tracking has emerged as a promising non-invasive approach to Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) screening, with systematic differences in attentional allocation and revisit behaviors observed during socially interactive tasks. Existing computational methods typically characterize eye-movements using discrete gaze trajectories and fixation events, yielding representations dominated by short-range temporal dynamics and limiting models that primarily emphasize long-range dependencies. Meanwhile, gaze behavior is naturally organized across semantically meaningful Areas of Interest (AOIs), whose attention allocation and transitions provide important structural cues, yet their relationships are rarely modeled explicitly. To address these limitations, we propose a structural face AOI-guided Eye-Gaze Track Network (AOI-Net) that jointly models short-term temporal dynamics and AOI-level structural organization. A network gating mechanism adaptively integrates the complementary temporal and structural representations according to their contributions to gaze-behavior characterization. To mitigate the pronounced class imbalance commonly encountered between individuals with ASD and Typically Developing (TD) participants in clinical datasets, class-distribution-aware learning is further employed to facilitate discriminative embedding learning under skewed class distributions. Experiments on a unique and large-scale clinical eye-tracking database comprising eight stimulus subsets and more than 1,300 participants show that AOI-Net consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods. The proposed framework also enables interpretable gaze-behavior modeling and provides a practical basis for scalable AI-driven ASD screening in real-world healthcare. The code is available at https://github.com/Zhanpei-ai/CIM-AOI-Net/tree/main/Code

title: Development of an Autonomous AI Coding Agent using Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) and Gemini LLM Frameworks
abstract: The ongoing changes in software engineering requirements have created a substantial need for automated tools which can create secure source code from natural language input. The performance of traditional Large Language Models (LLMs) becomes limited by their "one-shot" capability which results in logical hallucinations together with reduced algorithmic performance during complicated operations. The research presents an autonomous AI Coding Agent which establishes a connection between LLM-generated content and production-ready software through its organized methodology for decision making. Our framework uses the Gemini 2.5 Flash API for essential reasoning capabilities while employing a tailored Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) method to solve code generation challenges as a search operation. The agent uses a "Self-Critic" evaluator system to test different implementation methods which it ranks according to their accuracy and difficulty level before it improves its operational framework through backpropagation. The system operates through a Flask-based web interface which delivers instant feedback together with syntax highlighting features. Our experimental results show that the MCTS-based method achieves a 92% success rate on complex logical prompts while surpassing standard zero-shot generation models.

title: Detecting and Repairing Hallucinations in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Language models increasingly answer questions by consulting retrieved documents rather than memory alone, a design now common in search assistants and enterprise knowledge tools. Grounding a model in retrieved text reduces unsupported statements but does not eliminate them, and a reader cannot tell a grounded sentence from an invented one. Most research on this problem stops at detection, yet flagging a faulty answer changes nothing for the person reading it, and little is known about which action should follow. Using RAGTruth, a benchmark whose unsupported passages are annotated by hand, we split each flagged answer into individual factual claims, check each against the retrieved source, and compare leaving the answer untouched with three repair strategies of increasing richness: deleting an unsupported claim, replacing it with source text, and rewriting it. Three language models from different families judge the 916 repaired answers. Every strategy reduces the proportion of answers judged to contain unsupported content, and all three judges agree on the ordering. Deletion achieves the largest reduction while retaining least of the original answer, at 64.3% of the text, whereas rewriting retains 80.1% and reduces least. Repair is not confined to faulty answers: 83.5% of answers annotated clean are edited too. The strategies occupy different points on a grounding preservation trade-off rather than forming a quality ranking, and choosing between them needs evidence about answer usefulness that automatic metrics cannot supply.

title: Chat-Edit-3D++: Interactive 3D and 4D Scene Editing via Large Language Models
abstract: Recent work on image content manipulation based on vision-language pre-training models has been effectively extended to text-driven 3D scene editing. However, existing schemes for 3D scene editing still have certain shortcomings, hindering their further development as interactive design tools. Such schemes typically adhere to fixed input patterns, limiting flexibility in text input. Furthermore, their editing capabilities are constrained by a single or a few 2D visual models and require intricate pipeline design to integrate these models into 3D reconstruction processes. To address the aforementioned issues, we propose the Hash-Atlas network, which reformulates 3D scene editing as operations on 2D atlas images, thereby achieving a workflow decoupling of the 2D editing and 3D reconstruction processes. Building on this foundation, we introduce a dialogue-based 3D scene editing approach, termed CE3D++, which is centered on a large language model (LLM) that allows arbitrary textual input from users and interprets their intentions, subsequently facilitating the autonomous invocation of the corresponding visual models. Additionally, we extend CE3D++ to monocular 4D scenes by imposing motion constraints on moving objects and further fine-tuning the LLM by creating a trajectory dataset related to editing tasks, which enables the smaller LLM to schedule up to 30 different visual tools accurately. Experimental results demonstrate that CE3D++ effectively integrates multiple visual models to achieve diverse visual editing effects, possessing strong scene comprehension and multi-round dialog capabilities. The source codes and trained models are available at https://github.com/Fangkang515/CE3D.

title: Formal Verification and Dynamic Software Refactoring: A Collaborative Engine
abstract: This paper presents a novel collaborative engine designed to synergistically integrate formal verification and dynamic software refactoring. The core claim is that combining these two techniques can lead to continuous and optimized software quality. The proposed mechanism involves constructing an engine that leverages the conclusions of formal verification to guide dynamic refactoring processes while simultaneously verifying the correctness of the resulting changes. Current software development practices often treat formal verification and dynamic refactoring as separate, sequential activities. This disconnect hinders effective quality management. Our collaborative engine addresses this limitation by establishing a closed-loop system, offering a streamlined approach to improve software reliability and maintainability. This work outlines the engine's architecture, key components, and the methodology for achieving this synergistic effect. The paper emphasizes the practical benefits of this approach, demonstrating how it can significantly reduce software defects and enhance the overall development lifecycle.

title: Topological Protection of Quantum Information Against Decoherence
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of topological protection to mitigate decoherence in quantum information processing. The core claim centers around leveraging the robustness of topological states to significantly extend the coherence times of quantum information, thereby effectively suppressing decoherence. The proposed mechanism involves designing encoding schemes within topologically protected quantum systems, exploiting the inherent resilience of topological abnormal states against localized noise. Traditional quantum coding methods rely heavily on external protection, which often proves inefficient. This research demonstrates a paradigm shift by utilizing intrinsic physical properties to achieve genuine quantum information safeguarding. We explore theoretical frameworks and mathematical models to illustrate this approach, focusing on the fundamental principles and potential applications. The goal is to provide a robust foundation for developing future quantum technologies.

title: Probability Geometric Information Theory
abstract: This paper introduces Probability Geometric Information Theory (PGIT), a novel framework for efficiently computing and storing information, particularly in high-dimensional probabilistic spaces and non-linear information systems. The core concept is to leverage the dynamic nature of probability distributions to optimize information storage and retrieval. We propose a method based on iterative optimization and probabilistic computation to achieve significant improvements in data processing speed and efficiency compared to traditional approaches. The paper details the theoretical foundations, algorithmic implementation, and experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of PGIT. This work offers a new perspective on information theory, potentially revolutionizing data management and analysis.

title: Based on Formal Languages: Program Verification and Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the application of formal languages – specifically, description logics and type theories – to the domain of program verification and optimization. The core claim is that rigorous verification and optimization of software can be significantly enhanced by representing programs within the precise and traceable framework offered by these formal systems. The mechanism relies on translating program logic into a formal representation, subsequently employing formal verification techniques and optimization strategies. Unlike traditional methods that often rely on heuristics and experience, this approach leverages the inherent properties of formal languages to improve both the efficiency and reliability of the verification and optimization processes. The research investigates the feasibility and potential benefits of this paradigm shift, focusing on the ability to generate provably correct and optimized code. The paper outlines key concepts and techniques, highlighting the potential for a more robust and reliable software development lifecycle. ---

title: 基于动态自适应的概率空间优化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for probability space optimization, termed Dynamic Adaptive Probability Space Optimization (DAPSO). DAPSO leverages a dynamic parameter adjustment mechanism to enhance optimization efficiency, particularly in complex and high-dimensional problems. The core idea is to dynamically adjust the parameters of the probability space based on the problem characteristics and the learning process. This adaptive approach allows the optimizer to focus its efforts on the most relevant regions of the solution space, leading to improved convergence and faster solution times. We present a theoretical analysis demonstrating the effectiveness of this framework, showcasing its superior performance compared to traditional optimization methods on several benchmark datasets. The paper details the implementation of the dynamic parameter adjustment algorithm and discusses its impact on key optimization metrics, including convergence rate and solution quality. Furthermore, we provide a detailed analysis of the framework's robustness and potential for generalization.

title: Non-Linear Adaptive Clustering Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel non-linear adaptive clustering algorithm designed to address the limitations of traditional clustering methods. The algorithm dynamically adjusts the strength of cluster centers based on the underlying data relationships, leading to more accurate and interpretable cluster results. The core mechanism leverages non-linear transformations to effectively capture and model these relationships, offering a significant improvement in clustering performance compared to existing approaches. This research focuses on enhancing the robustness and interpretability of clustering by enabling the algorithm to adapt to varying data characteristics. The proposed algorithm demonstrates improved performance on several benchmark datasets, providing a robust solution for complex data analysis and visualization.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: Adaptive Hyperparameter Optimization
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) offers the potential to revolutionize various computational tasks, particularly in optimization problems. This paper explores the application of QML to adaptive hyperparameter optimization, a crucial step in training machine learning models. We propose a novel QML-based algorithm that leverages quantum state dynamics to automatically adjust hyperparameters, leading to improved model performance. This approach addresses the limitations of traditional static hyperparameter optimization methods by dynamically responding to the data and model itself. The core mechanism involves the quantum state evolution driven by the learning process, enabling a more efficient and robust optimization process. This work demonstrates the potential of QML to significantly enhance model accuracy and generalization capabilities.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Probabilistic Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a peculiar phenomenon in quantum mechanics, offers a fundamentally different approach to computation and information processing. This paper introduces a novel probabilistic algorithm predicated on the utilization of quantum entanglement to enhance numerical simulation and optimization capabilities. The core mechanism centers around leveraging entanglement to introduce a non-classical computational process, resulting in increased accuracy and the ability to navigate a broader range of solution spaces. This work explores the potential of entanglement to overcome limitations imposed by traditional computational methods, presenting a new framework for probabilistic algorithms with significant implications for scientific and engineering applications.

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Intrinsic Motivation and Cooperative Reward Shaping
abstract: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) offers a promising approach to tackling complex cooperative tasks. However, existing MARL algorithms often fail to achieve robust coordination and cooperation, primarily due to difficulties in learning effective joint policies and the lack of mechanisms to encourage collaborative behavior. This paper proposes a novel framework that integrates intrinsic motivation and cooperative reward shaping into a MARL system. The core idea is to augment the traditional extrinsic reward signal with internal drives, such as curiosity and competence, and to shape the reward function to explicitly incentivize cooperation among agents. We introduce a framework where agents learn to maximize both their external rewards and their internal motivation levels, while simultaneously benefiting from a carefully designed cooperative reward structure. The theoretical analysis demonstrates the potential of this approach to overcome the limitations of standard MARL and to promote more efficient and stable cooperative learning. We present a detailed description of the framework and discuss its key components, highlighting the interplay between intrinsic motivation, cooperative reward shaping, and the overall learning process. The results, although presented without empirical experimentation, illustrate the potential impact of this approach on improving cooperative MARL performance. ---

We present a detailed description of the framework and discuss its key components, highlighting the interplay between intrinsic motivation, cooperative reward shaping, and the overall learning process. The results, although presented without empirical experimentation, illustrate the potential impact of this approach on improving cooperative MARL performance. ---

title: On Information-Theoretic Program Execution Path Optimization
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to program execution path optimization by leveraging concepts from information theory. The core idea is to treat program execution paths as information streams, quantifying their complexity and potential for optimization using metrics like entropy and cross-entropy. We propose a framework utilizing greedy or dynamic programming algorithms to identify and select optimal execution paths, aiming to minimize execution time. This work presents a fundamentally new perspective on program optimization, particularly beneficial for programs with intricate execution paths. The methodology offers a potential route towards more efficient and adaptive program execution, driven by an information-theoretic understanding of program complexity. ---

title: Towards Secure Prompt Processing: A Unified Framework to Detect, Sanitize, and Prevent Adversarial Prompts via Dual-optimized Threshold-aware Learning
abstract: In the modern era, Large Language Models (LLMs) are a cornerstone in the creation of intelligent systems, boasting significant capabilities in various fields.Adversarial prompts continue to pose a significant threat to LLM security, as they exploit the lack of distinction between trusted and malicious prompts.Such weaknesses are extremely critical to the trustworthiness, safety, and reliability of real-world implements.To tackle this, this study introduces a sanitization and high-confidence inference for effective LLM defense through isolation and neutralization gateway (SHIELDING), which consists of linguistic feature extraction, sentiment-based analysis, and a Threshold-aware Random Forest (TRF) classifier.The TRF model is designed to include class-specific threshold optimized via Crested Porcupine Optimizer (CPO), allowing the model to adaptively make decisions.The experimental results indicate that the proposed method has good performance with an accuracy of 99%, a classification Attack Success Rate (ASR) of 0.656%, and a real ASR of 3.994% showing that it is an effective method to improve the security of LLM.

title: PERSIST: Persistent-State Discrimination for Shot Boundary Detection
abstract: Shot boundary detection (SBD) is widely treated as the localisation of local visual discontinuities, yet many false positives such as hand-held shake, illumination flicker, motion blur, occlusion, and damaged archival material produce equally sharp local change without introducing a new shot. We reformulate SBD as boundary semantic discrimination: a frame is favoured as a boundary only when its local change evidence is accompanied by a persistent update of the video's latent temporal state, rather than a transient excursion that returns to the surrounding trend. This persistence test is operationalised with a continuous latent state from a FiLM-conditioned sinusoidal representation network and a structured discriminator that combines three semantic cues, local change, transient impulse, and return-to-trend, into a single interpretable per-frame signal over a dual-rate temporal backbone. The resulting framework, PERSIST, turns every decision into an inspectable one: the persistence criterion is trained into the classifier, its per-frame effect stays readable from the gate triple, and its learned latent state is measurably boundary-discriminative. On a 2,727-video per-subtype diagnostic it removes 33-80% of flash, text-overlay, and archival false positives relative to an identically trained cue detector, and at matched true-transition recall it roughly halves TransNetV2's pseudo-event false positives on that diagnostic and cuts its false positives on ClipShots footage by about a quarter, while preserving recall. It does so while reaching parity with the strongest public detector across online, broadcast, short-form, and historical-archive transfer evaluations, under markedly stricter training: it learns from ClipShots real transitions only, whereas the anchor draws on additional corpora whose transitions are 85% synthetic. Code is available at https://github.com/linty5/PERSIST.

title: Titans-QFWP: A Regime-Aware Hybrid Quantum Fast Weight Programmer for Portfolio Optimization
abstract: We propose Titans-QFWP, a hybrid reinforcement learning architecture integrating a Quantum Fast Weight Programmer with Titans-style memory (Persistence, Surprise, and Forgetting) for adaptive portfolio optimization. To address high-dimensional market features, we introduce an enhanced A3C^2 framework with Hungarian-aligned K-means clustering and scaled log-return rewards. Evaluated on 468 S&P 500 stocks under an Equal-Parameter-Count (EPC) benchmark with approximately 3,000 trainable parameters, Titans-QFWP achieves strong performance (median ARR 0.4260, Calmar 8.5504, IR 0.8427). Ablation results reveal that quantum gating fundamentally reshapes memory component roles, with Persistence supporting drawdown control, Surprise contributing to return generation, and Forgetting providing additional stabilization. By stabilizing these quantum representations, the model enables defensive allocation during market drawdowns while preserving upside potential.

title: Quantum discord of Gaussian states in non-inertial frames
abstract: We investigate the redistribution of continuous-variable Gaussian quantum discord under the Unruh effect for both one and two uniformly accelerated observers. The discord shared between the inertial mode and the accessible accelerated mode, as well as that between the two accessible accelerated modes, decays monotonically with acceleration and vanishes in the limit $a\to\infty$, while the Unruh effect generates discord in all causally disconnected Rindler mode pairs. The initial quantum correlation is therefore redistributed across Rindler partitions rather than destroyed. We further characterize how the squeezing parameter $s$ and field frequency $ω$ control the discord in different mode-pair classes. For causally connected pairs, $s$ and $ω$ exert comparable, interchangeable effects; for cross-region pairs, the squeezing parameter dominates; and for intra-observer cross-region pairs, the field frequency is more influential. In the two-observer case, the $A_{II}$-$B_{II}$ pair exhibits non-monotonic behavior with a peak whose position shifts to larger $a$ as $ω$ increases, and both parameters contribute only weakly except near an optimal $\fracω{s}$ ratio.

title: ToriLearn: An AI Enabled Adaptive Learning System for GCE Chemistry Preparation
abstract: Secondary school students preparing for the General Certificate of Education examinations in Cameroon face a documented 62 percent failure rate in core science subjects, alongside heavy reliance on static revision material that does not adjust to what a learner already knows. This paper presents the design and implementation of ToriLearn, a prototype web based adaptive learning platform built to address this gap for GCE Ordinary Level Chemistry. The system combines a React and TypeScript frontend with a Django REST Framework backend organised into four layers, namely presentation, API, application logic, and data persistence. Within the application layer, a Bayesian Knowledge Tracing engine estimates mastery of eleven Chemistry knowledge components in real time, a Gradient Boosting classifier recommends chapter level progression, a K-Means clustering module groups learners by behaviour, and a conversa-tional tutor built on Groq hosted large language models supplies explanations with an offline fallback chain. The system was built across five Agile Scrum sprints and evaluated through functional testing, performance benchmarking on a local development server, and mathematical simulation of three learner trajectories. Results show that all core modules function correctly, that the adaptive quiz endpoint responds within 45 to 80 milliseconds under development conditions, and that the simulated learner scenarios behave in a manner consistent with the underlying Bayesian model. No live classroom pilot was conducted, so claims in this paper are limited to architectural soundness and simulated behaviour rather than measured learning gains. We discuss how this layered, fallback aware design compares with existing intelligent tutoring architectures and outline what a subsequent classroom deployment would need to confirm.

title: The Label Moves the Reading: Entity-Name Leakage in Language-Model Dimensional Ratings of a Fixed Text
abstract: A dimensional rating produced by a language model over a written artifact is normally treated as a reading of that artifact. This study shows it is not purely that. Holding an artifact byte-identical and exchanging only the entity name it concerns, an eight-dimensional profile moved by .55 to .82 rubric points per dimension across two independently designed collections, at or above the same operators' test-retest spread in every run, over 1,057 records from six operators in three model families. The deflationary account – that the effect registers incongruity between a text written for one entity and a label naming another – is refuted: texts authored for no entity produced a larger effect, .824 against .584. The movement is structured rather than diffuse, the largest and smallest dimensions differing by a factor of 2.4 with both extremes reproducing across runs. Which of three routes carries the leakage is not identified, and the study reports why rather than resolving it: a re-analysis shows the neutrality guard that blocked the decomposition referred its interaction to the entity main effect rather than the within-cell residual, and the class effect is roughly half a percent of total variance, so that ratio is a ratio of two small quantities. Referred correctly, the interaction is roughly five percent of residual. The exchange procedure is offered as a diagnostic other rubric instruments can be put through. Includes zharnikov-2026bp-entity-name-leakage.yaml (Paper Spec v0.1.0) – a machine-readable specification of the paper's claims, assumptions, and dependencies. The paper's full machine-first bundle (the SPINE claim/dependency graph and the ONTOLOGY term module) lives in the public repository; see https://github.com/spectralbranding/paper-spec for the standard. This PDF is generated programmatically from that machine-first source under a research-as-repository model.

title: Nonlinear Model Parameter Optimization via Dynamic Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to non-linear model parameter optimization utilizing a dynamic optimization framework. The core challenge in many real-world applications is finding optimal model parameters that accurately represent the underlying data. Traditional parameter optimization methods often rely on manually tuned parameters, which can be time-consuming and may not always yield the best results. We introduce a dynamic optimization algorithm that automatically adjusts model parameters based on a complex model analysis, aiming to improve both prediction accuracy and generalization ability. The algorithm incorporates a "dynamic parameter" mechanism that iteratively refines parameter values to achieve a more optimal configuration. This approach offers a significant improvement over existing methods, particularly in scenarios with complex, non-linear models. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed dynamic optimization framework through rigorous analysis and simulated results.

title: Self-Organizing Semantic Networks
abstract: This paper explores the concept of Self-Organizing Semantic Networks (SOSN), a novel approach to knowledge representation and reasoning. Traditional semantic networks are static, requiring manual design and refinement. We propose a system, the Meta-Network Weaver, which dynamically creates and evolves a network based on data analysis, achieving self-organizing properties. This system aims to improve knowledge representation by automatically adjusting connections and creating a more flexible and adaptable structure. The paper details the design and implementation of the Meta-Network Weaver, highlighting its key mechanisms and demonstrating its potential benefits through a simulated case study.

title: Quantum Potential Simulation of Adaptive Topological Structure Adjustment
abstract: Quantum potential simulation offers a powerful tool for modeling complex quantum systems, particularly those exhibiting topological properties. However, traditional approaches often struggle with the computational cost of accurately capturing topological features. This paper introduces a novel method for quantum potential simulation that dynamically adjusts the quantum potential field to enhance the simulation's accuracy and efficiency. We propose a self-adaptive topology adjustment algorithm, which iteratively optimizes the quantum potential based on the system's state. This approach leverages quantum state learning to achieve significant improvements in simulation fidelity and speed, offering a promising path toward more efficient and precise quantum simulations.

title: Title: Bayesian Statistical Resonance – Predictive Modeling of Mathematical Structure
abstract: This research investigates the potential for Bayesian statistical resonance – a novel approach to modeling the statistical dependence inherent in mathematical structures – to predict the emergence of new mathematical theorems and concepts. Traditional statistical methods often struggle to capture the complex, non-linear dependencies that drive innovation in mathematics. This work proposes a Bayesian framework specifically designed to identify these subtle correlations, offering a predictive capability exceeding existing techniques. The core mechanism centers on a modified Bayesian network that incorporates non-linear relationships and dynamically adjusts its parameters based on observed data, fostering a feedback loop that anticipates future mathematical developments. This research aims to move beyond simple pattern recognition and towards a deeper understanding of the underlying mathematical structure, ultimately providing a powerful tool for mathematical discovery.

title: 自适应的变量空间拓扑的量子计算应用
abstract: This paper investigates the application of adaptive variable space topology in quantum computation, aiming to enhance precision and efficiency in large-data processing. We introduce a novel dynamic topology design, dynamically adjusting the topology based on data characteristics, and leveraging this adaptation to improve computational accuracy. The core mechanism centers on exploiting the inherent properties of quantum topology to optimize complex calculations. The study demonstrates the potential of this approach to overcome limitations of traditional optimization techniques, particularly in scenarios involving high-dimensional data. This work presents a framework for automatically adapting variable space topologies, offering a significant advancement in the design of quantum algorithms.

title: Title: Dynamic Topology-Based Constraint Modeling in Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic topology-based constraint modeling mechanism for evolutionary algorithms, aiming to enhance the exploration of the solution space and improve convergence. Traditional evolutionary algorithms often fix the topology of constraint networks, limiting the search space. We propose a feedback loop that dynamically adjusts topology based on solution quality, providing a mechanism for adaptive exploration. The system incorporates a monitoring mechanism that assesses solution quality and iteratively refines the topology to guide the algorithm toward more promising regions of the solution space. This approach addresses a significant limitation of current evolutionary algorithms, offering a potentially more effective and robust method for finding optimal solutions. The core mechanism involves a continuous assessment of solution quality and a corresponding topology adjustment, ensuring a dynamic and adaptive exploration strategy.

title: Contextual Symbolic Regression with Latent Semantic Analysis
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to symbolic regression, termed Contextual Symbolic Regression with Latent Semantic Analysis (CSR-LSA). Traditional symbolic regression methods often struggle with complex datasets exhibiting underlying semantic relationships, leading to inaccurate or computationally expensive model discovery. CSR-LSA addresses this limitation by leveraging Latent Semantic Analysis (LSA) to uncover these relationships, reducing the dimensionality of the data while preserving essential semantic information. The resulting latent representation is then used as the operational space for symbolic regression, significantly improving model accuracy and efficiency. We demonstrate the effectiveness of CSR-LSA through theoretical analysis and a detailed discussion of the methodology. The core contribution lies in the synergistic combination of symbolic regression's ability to generate equations and LSA's capability to extract hidden semantic structures. The proposed method offers a promising direction for automated model discovery in various domains, particularly those with rich contextual data.

title: Quantum-Inspired Reservoir Computing with Temporal Encoding
abstract: Reservoir computing (RC) has emerged as a powerful technique for processing time-series data, particularly in applications demanding real-time response. However, traditional RC often suffers from limitations in sensitivity to temporal changes and adaptability to evolving data patterns. This paper proposes a novel approach—Quantum-Inspired Reservoir Computing with Temporal Encoding (QIRCTE)—which integrates principles inspired by quantum measurement theory to enhance the performance of RC. The core idea is to encode temporal information directly into the reservoir's state space, creating a more efficient and robust processing unit. This is achieved through a modified reservoir architecture and a specific learning rule. We demonstrate, theoretically, that this temporal encoding significantly improves the reservoir's ability to capture and respond to transient signals, mirroring aspects of quantum measurement's ability to reveal underlying correlations. The theoretical framework is presented with mathematical derivations, including the state-space equations and the modified learning rule. We outline the key elements of the QIRCTE architecture and discuss potential applications, highlighting its advantages over conventional RC methods.

evidence.title: Quantum-Inspired Reservoir Computing with Temporal Encoding
evidence.abstract: Reservoir computing (RC) has emerged as a powerful technique for processing time-series data, particularly in applications demanding real-time response. However, traditional RC often suffers from limitations in sensitivity to temporal changes and adaptability to evolving data patterns. This paper proposes a novel approach—Quantum-Inspired Reservoir Computing with Temporal Encoding (QIRCTE)—which integrates principles inspired by quantum measurement theory to enhance the performance of RC. The core idea is to encode temporal information directly into the reservoir's state space, creating a more efficient and robust processing unit. This is achieved through a modified reservoir architecture and a specific learning rule. We demonstrate, theoretically, that this temporal encoding significantly improves the reservoir's ability to capture and respond to transient signals, mirroring aspects of quantum measurement's ability to reveal underlying correlations. The theoretical framework is presented with mathematical derivations, including the state-space equations and the modified learning rule. We outline the key elements of the QIRCTE architecture and discuss potential applications, highlighting its advantages over conventional RC methods.

title: Self-Adaptive Variable Space Graph Modeling
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive variable space graph modeling technique, designed to enhance model generalization by dynamically adjusting the structure of the variable space graph based on input data characteristics. The proposed model utilizes a learning-based approach to optimize the graph's parameters, allowing for automated feature-driven adjustments. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through a series of experiments comparing its performance against existing approaches on several benchmark datasets. The core mechanism centers around a self-tuning parameter adjustment process that adapts to the data's inherent patterns. The paper concludes with a detailed overview of the model's architecture, key improvements, and future research directions.

title: An Explainable XGBoost Framework for Mortality Prediction in People Living with HIV Receiving Antiretroviral Therapy
abstract: Mortality remains an important concern among people living with HIV (PLHIV) receiving antiretroviral therapy (ART), particularly when high-risk patients are not identified early. This study presents an explainable mortality prediction approach based on an optimized Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) classifier. A retrospective dataset containing 393 clinical records was analyzed. Before model training, duplicate entries were removed, missing values were imputed, categorical variables were encoded, and class imbalance in the training data was addressed using the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE). Optuna was employed to determine suitable XGBoost hyperparameters, while SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to examine how individual predictors affected the model output. Performance was evaluated on an independent testing set using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC). The resulting classifier achieved an accuracy of 89.87%, weighted precision of 0.91, weighted recall of 0.90, weighted F1-score of 0.90, and an ROC-AUC of 0.948. For the mortality class, recall reached 0.97, with 30 of 31 mortality cases correctly detected. Follow-up duration and functional status contributed most strongly to the predictions. SHAP analysis further showed whether these predictors shifted individual outputs toward mortality or survival. The integration of optimized predictive modeling with explainable artificial intelligence enabled accurate mortality prediction while providing transparent insight into how individual predictors influenced the model output. The findings suggest that the model may assist in identifying patients who require closer monitoring, although validation using external and multicenter data is necessary before clinical implementation.

title: Beyond Accuracy: A Reproducible Framework for Detecting Data Leakage and Shortcut Learning in Machine Learning Pipelines Toward Trustworthy, Reproducible, and Sustainable AI Systems
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly deployed in high-impact domains such as healthcare, cybersecurity, autonomous systems, and industrial decision-making, where reliable model evaluation is essential. Despite continuous improvements in predictive performance, growing evidence indicates that many reported gains are inflated by methodological flaws, including data leakage, shortcut learning, dataset shift, and insufficient reproducibility practices. These issues compromise model generalization, reduce robustness, and undermine trust in AI systems. This study proposes a reproducible, leakage-aware evaluation framework designed to detect and quantify methodological risks throughout the machine learning pipeline. The framework integrates four complementary dimensions: dataset integrity analysis, pipeline validation, robustness assessment under controlled perturbations, and reproducibility evaluation. These components are consolidated into a novel Leakage Risk Score (LRS), a normalized metric that estimates methodological risk and complements conventional performance measures such as accuracy. A proof-of-concept evaluation using multiple supervised classification datasets under clean and intentionally contaminated conditions shows that data leakage consistently inflates predictive performance while reducing robustness and reproducibility. Although the empirical validation is intentionally illustrative, the proposed framework establishes a unified foundation for leakage-aware evaluation and supports the transition from benchmark-oriented assessment toward trustworthy, reproducible, and sustainable AI systems.

title: Hybrid deep learning approach with capsule networks for financial fraud detection
abstract: The rapid growth of digital financial services has significantly increased the complexity and volume of financial transactions, making the accurate detection of fraudulent activities a critical challenge for conventional machine learning approaches. This study proposes a hybrid intelligent fraud detection framework that integrates data preprocessing, feature selection, deep learning classification, and adaptive hyperparameter optimization to improve fraud detection accuracy while maintaining computational efficiency. Initially, transaction records are preprocessed through missing value treatment, feature normalization, outlier analysis, and Tomek Links undersampling to enhance data quality and address class imbalance. Subsequently, the Perfumer Optimization Algorithm (POA) is employed to identify the most informative feature subset, whereas a Capsule Network performs hierarchical feature representation learning to capture complex relationships among transaction attributes. The Fennec Fox Optimization Algorithm (FFOA) is further utilized to optimize the network hyperparameters, improving convergence and overall classification performance. The proposed framework was evaluated using a publicly available Kaggle financial fraud benchmark dataset and compared with several state-of-the-art deep learning models. Experimental results achieved an accuracy of 99.67%, precision of 99.52%, recall of 99.74%, F1-score of 99.65%, and an MCC of 0.993, while maintaining low computational complexity suitable for real-time applications. Furthermore, SHAP and permutation importance analyses demonstrated that behavioural attributes, particularly failed transaction attempts and transaction frequency, contributed most significantly to fraud prediction. The proposed framework advances financial fraud detection by combining optimization-driven feature selection, hierarchical representation learning, and adaptive hyperparameter tuning into a unified architecture, providing an accurate, interpretable, and computationally efficient solution suitable for next-generation intelligent financial security systems.

title: EviAnchor: Mitigating Hallucinations in Large Vision-Language Models via Regional Visual Evidence Compensation
abstract: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) frequently generate content unsupported by visual inputs. Preliminary experiments show that visual evidence is primarily incorporated into answer-side representations in early-to-middle decoder layers, while its direct influence progressively weakens in later layers. This attenuation suggests that visual evidence acquired earlier may be insufficiently utilized during subsequent generation. Based on this observation, we propose EviAnchor, a training-free and single-branch inference framework that preserves and reactivates visual evidence throughout generation. EviAnchor introduces Regional Evidence Anchor (REA) slots to progressively aggregate dense visual tokens into spatially structured representations. It then strengthens the current decision state's access to these visual anchors through decision-conditioned evidence routing, mitigating excessive dependence on textual context. Finally, the model resumes its native Transformer computation to integrate the retrieved visual evidence with question semantics and generation history. Experiments across POPE, CHAIR, and MMHal-Bench demonstrate consistent improvements in visual grounding.

title: Microseismic Weak Event Detection and First Arrival Picking Based on YOLOv8
abstract: Abstract：Weak event detection is a key step to improve the accuracy of first-arrival picking in microseismic monitoring.Traditional STA/LTA and AIC methods have limited detection capability under low signal-to-noise ratio conditions.This paper proposes a microseismic event detection method based on the YOLOv8 object detection model, which transforms event detection into a candidate-window object detection task.Experimental results show that YOLOv8 achieves an overall mAP50 of 0.948 on the test set, with a precision of 0.841, recall of 0.917, and mAP50 of 0.956 for weak events, and a false-detection rate of 0% on both types of negative samples.On this basis, a YOLOv8-detection-box-guided AIC joint first-arrival picking strategy is proposed.The detection box locates candidate event windows, within which the AIC function is computed for accurate picking, and multi-trace continuity constraints are further applied to improve the stability of the first-arrival picks.This method provides an effective technical solution for automated processing of low-SNR microseismic data.

title: Topology-Driven Parameter Optimization in Neural Networks
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to neural network parameter optimization utilizing topology-driven methods. Traditional parameter optimization relies on fixed, predefined configurations, often resulting in suboptimal performance and limited generalization. We propose a method where the network's structure is dynamically shaped by a topological analysis of the input data, allowing for adaptation and improvement. This framework leverages a novel topological representation to guide the network's evolution, leading to enhanced generalization and robustness. The core mechanism centers around a continuous, evolving topology that dynamically adjusts the network's layer arrangements and connections, optimizing for a specific objective function. The paper presents a methodology for constructing and applying such a topology, demonstrating its effectiveness through simulated experiments and initial analysis of a simplified neural network architecture.

title: ##基于图卷积神经网络的知识图谱推理
abstract: This paper explores the application of Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) for knowledge graph reasoning. Traditional knowledge graph reasoning methods often rely on rule-based systems, which can be brittle and difficult to scale. We propose a novel approach that leverages the power of deep learning, specifically GCNs, to learn representations of nodes and predict relationships within a knowledge graph. The core claim of this work is that utilizing GCNs significantly improves both the accuracy and efficiency of knowledge graph reasoning. The mechanism involves representing the knowledge graph as a graph structure and employing GCNs for node representation learning and relationship prediction. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a detailed analysis of the underlying mathematical framework and the potential for improved performance compared to conventional methods. The research contributes to a more robust and scalable approach to knowledge graph inference, offering a promising avenue for advancements in areas such as question answering, recommendation systems, and semantic understanding. ---

title: Quantum Error Correction Topological Neuron Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a novel architecture for neural networks leveraging the principles of quantum error correction (QEC) and topological codes. The core claim is that integrating these two fields offers a pathway to achieving unprecedented levels of fault tolerance and parallel computing capabilities. The proposed Quantum Error Correction Topological Neuron Networks (QETNNs) utilize a network topology based on topological codes, where information is encoded and protected by the inherent redundancy of the code. This approach mitigates the significant challenges associated with data transmission and error correction in traditional neural networks operating in quantum computing environments. The mechanism relies on encoding neural network weights and activations within the topological code, providing robust protection against decoherence and other sources of quantum noise. We outline the fundamental principles, explore the potential advantages, and discuss the key challenges associated with realizing QETNNs. The architecture's parallel data processing capabilities are a central focus, addressing the scalability limitations of current quantum neural networks. We present a theoretical framework and explore potential implementation strategies, highlighting the opportunity for significant advancements in both quantum computing and artificial intelligence.

title: 基于动态量子态的自适应算法设计
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm based on dynamic quantum state evolution, designed to enhance algorithm efficiency and accuracy through automated parameter adjustment. Traditional parameter adjustment methods often lack the ability to fully exploit the inherent dynamic behavior of quantum states. This algorithm leverages quantum state evolution to dynamically adjust algorithm parameters, enabling a more adaptive and robust approach to optimization. The core mechanism involves a continuous feedback loop that monitors and modifies the quantum state, optimizing the algorithm's performance in real-time. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of benchmark problems, showcasing significant improvements in both computational speed and solution accuracy compared to traditional methods. The proposed algorithm offers a promising avenue for accelerating complex optimization tasks in various fields.

title: 基于生物信息的量子态预测模型
abstract: This research investigates a novel quantum state prediction model predicated on the dynamic interplay of quantum states within biological molecules. Traditional methods often rely on complex physical models, limiting the ability to accurately predict quantum system behavior. This study proposes a new approach utilizing the inherent quantum fluctuations of biological molecules as a predictive mechanism, offering a potential paradigm shift in quantum device optimization. The core mechanism involves establishing a dynamic model that interprets biological molecular quantum state transitions, enabling the prediction of quantum system performance. The significance of this research lies in its potential to streamline the design and optimization of quantum devices by leveraging the fundamental properties of biological systems.

title: Adaptive Kernel Methods with Dynamic Feature Selection
abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive kernel method that dynamically selects features during the learning process, aiming to improve both the efficiency and accuracy of kernel methods. The core idea is to integrate a meta-learning component within the kernel framework. This component learns to predict the optimal feature subset based on the current data and kernel parameters. This adaptive approach mitigates the computational burden associated with traditional kernel methods, particularly in high-dimensional feature spaces, and effectively addresses the challenge of overfitting. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this methodology through a theoretical analysis and outline the key components and considerations for implementation. The resulting algorithm offers a compelling solution for scenarios where feature selection is crucial for optimal performance.

title: 基于量子纠缠的非线性拓扑结构匹配算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithm for non-linear topological structure matching based on quantum entanglement. Traditional methods often rely on manual design, limiting their applicability to complex topological structures. Our proposed algorithm leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to simulate and match topological structures with unprecedented accuracy. The core mechanism involves creating entangled states to represent and manipulate the topological relationships between different components of the structure. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through a series of simulations and initial experimental validation, highlighting its potential to significantly improve the accuracy of topological structure matching.

title: Probability Logistic Network Reconstruction Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm for reconstructing data distributions from complex probability logistic networks. Traditional methods often rely on computationally intensive numerical techniques, necessitating precise estimates of data distributions. We propose a new approach that leverages the inherent probabilistic nature of logistic networks, employing a direct inverse operation to estimate the original data distribution. This design aims to significantly reduce computational complexity and improve the accuracy of data distribution estimation. The core mechanism involves a carefully structured inverse operation that exploits the network's probability density function, eliminating intermediate steps and simplifying the reconstruction process. The algorithm demonstrates potential for substantial improvements in data distribution estimation, offering a more efficient and accurate solution compared to existing approaches.

title: Self-Adaptive Topological Deformation Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm, termed Self-Adaptive Topological Deformation (SADT) optimization, that leverages dynamic topology manipulation to achieve enhanced optimization performance. Traditional optimization algorithms often rely on static transformations, limiting their adaptability to complex, dynamic systems. SADT dynamically adjusts the topology of the optimization landscape, allowing the algorithm to respond to changes in the problem context. The core mechanism of the algorithm involves a series of iterative adjustments to the transformation parameters, guided by a feedback loop that continuously evaluates the effectiveness of the topology changes. The algorithm is designed to be robust and adaptable to a wide range of problem types, offering a significant improvement over existing approaches. We present a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's performance, demonstrating its effectiveness in several benchmark problems across diverse domains. The proposed method offers a promising pathway toward more efficient and robust optimization solutions.

title: A quantum let within the lambda calculus
abstract: Since the seminal work of Selinger and Valiron, the standard design for quantum lambda calculi has kept the quantum state outside the program: terms manipulate pointers to an external register. This is largely due to the difficulty of eliminating tensor products. For example, the calculus $λ_ρ^\circ$ embeds density matrices directly within terms, where terms carry the entire computation state, a feature particularly appealing for program verification. However, lacking a tensor elimination construct, it can neither access the individual qubits of a compound state nor discard them. Borgna showed that this inability to discard qubits makes the calculus strictly less expressive than the quantum lambda calculus of Selinger and Valiron. In this paper we show that tensor elimination is possible in this setting. The key observation is that the Pauli decomposition, combined with the spectral decomposition of the Pauli matrices, allows any $n$-qubit density matrix to be expressed as a real linear combination of tensor products of single-qubit density matrices. Exploiting this fact, we extend $λ_ρ^\circ$ with a construct $\mathrm{let}\ x^{\otimes n} = ρ \mathrm{in}\ t$, which binds each $x_i$ to a single-qubit density matrix arising from the decomposition of $ρ$. We equip the extended calculus with a rewrite system, a type system, and a denotational semantics, and prove Subject Reduction, Progress, Strong Normalisation, Soundness, and Adequacy. The new construct also recovers the missing ability to discard qubits, thereby restoring expressiveness. Moreover, we show that this is achieved in a physically principled way: a variable unused in $t$ is interpreted exactly as being partial-traced out, as dictated by the no-deleting theorem. We illustrate the resulting compositionality through quantum teleportation and the three-qubit bit-flip code.

For example, the calculus $λ_ρ^\circ$ embeds density matrices directly within terms, where terms carry the entire computation state, a feature particularly appealing for program verification. However, lacking a tensor elimination construct, it can neither access the individual qubits of a compound state nor discard them. Borgna showed that this inability to discard qubits makes the calculus strictly less expressive than the quantum lambda calculus of Selinger and Valiron. In this paper we show that tensor elimination is possible in this setting. The key observation is that the Pauli decomposition, combined with the spectral decomposition of the Pauli matrices, allows any $n$-qubit density matrix to be expressed as a real linear combination of tensor products of single-qubit density matrices. Exploiting this fact, we extend $λ_ρ^\circ$ with a construct $\mathrm{let}\ x^{\otimes n} = ρ \mathrm{in}\ t$, which binds each $x_i$ to a single-qubit density matrix arising from the decomposition of $ρ$. We equip the extended calculus with a rewrite system, a type system, and a denotational semantics, and prove Subject Reduction, Progress, Strong Normalisation, Soundness, and Adequacy. The new construct also recovers the missing ability to discard qubits, thereby restoring expressiveness. Moreover, we show that this is achieved in a physically principled way: a variable unused in $t$ is interpreted exactly as being partial-traced out, as dictated by the no-deleting theorem. We illustrate the resulting compositionality through quantum teleportation and the three-qubit bit-flip code.

title: 3D-MRL: Nested Multimodal 3D Representations via Matryoshka Representation Learning
abstract: Vision-Language Models align point clouds with image and text embeddings, enabling zero-shot recognition, retrieval, and open-vocabulary understanding of 3D shapes. Existing multimodal 3D pre-training methods produce fixed-dimensional embeddings, requiring separate models for different computational budgets. We propose 3D Matryoshka Representation Learning (3D-MRL), a multimodal 3D pre-training framework based on Matryoshka Representation Learning. 3D-MRL learns nested 3D representations by aligning point clouds with frozen CLIP image and text embeddings while applying contrastive supervision across multiple embedding dimensions. The Matryoshka objective is applied only to the 3D encoder, allowing a single model to produce representations at different dimensionalities without retraining. Experiments on the Objaverse-LVIS, ModelNet40, and ScanNet datasets show that 3D-MRL achieves competitive performance on zero-shot and few-shot 3D recognition tasks. In addition, the learned representations support retrieval across different embedding dimensions within a single model. On Objaverse-LVIS, 3D-MRL improves Top-1 accuracy from 46.8% to 50.9%. Retrieval experiments further show that different embedding dimensions yield varying levels of semantic and geometric specificity.

title: HANIA: Planner-Guided Multimodal Graph Evidence Selection for Grounded Question Answering
abstract: Multimodal question answering remains sensitive to noisy, incomplete, and weakly grounded evidence. Long unstructured contexts can introduce redundancy and encourage unsupported generation, while flat retrieval may overlook relations needed for multi-step reasoning. We present HANIA, a planner-guided multimodal graph framework for evidence-grounded question answering. HANIA processes the supplied image and text using a frozen vision-language model to extract concise question-relevant visual evidence with explicit abstention. It then constructs an input-grounded multimodal graph and applies a two-group finite-state planner to coordinate descriptive and relational evidence. Coverage-aware pruning retains a compact evidence set based on relevance, graph confidence, concept coverage, and modality diversity. The selected passages, visual statements, and graph triples are provided to a frozen instruction-tuned decoder. We evaluate HANIA on ScienceQA using answer accuracy, evidence-filtering quality, evidence-budget sensitivity, and efficiency. The results show that structured evidence planning and compact graph-guided retrieval can support competitive multimodal question answering without target-dataset fine-tuning or iterative retrieval. The code is available at https://github.com/Zafar-southeast/HANIA.

title: WSI feature, BRACS, CPTAC, CAMELYON16, CAMELYON17
abstract: This dataset contains pre-extracted whole-slide image (WSI) features for four pathology benchmarks: CAMELYON16 (C16), CAMELYON17 (C17), BRACS, and CPTAC. Features are extracted from image patches using two different encoders: (1) a ResNet-18 pretrained on ImageNet, and (2) a self-supervised Vision Transformer (ViT) pretrained on histopathology whole-slide images. These features are provided to facilitate reproducible evaluation of multiple-instance learning (MIL) methods without requiring users to repeat computationally expensive WSI preprocessing and feature extraction.

title: Beyond True and False: A Narrative Review of Non-Classical Logics, from Intuitionism to Paraconsistency
abstract: Classical logic's laws---excluded middle, non-contradiction, the monotonicity of truth---were long held to be the laws of reason itself, and the twentieth century's non-classical logics are the demonstration that they are choices, each with rivals that are coherent, useful, and in some settings truer to the phenomena. This article presents a narrative review of the primary literature of the three great non-classical programs, from Brouwer's intuitionism and formalism and Kolmogorov's rejection of the excluded middle, which founded the intuitionistic challenge to classical reasoning, through Heyting's formal rules of intuitionistic logic, Godel's interpretation of the intuitionistic calculus, Kripke's semantical analyses of intuitionistic and modal logic, which gave the new logics their model theory, Lewis and Langford's symbolic logic and its modal systems, and Anderson and Belnap's entailment program of relevance, to the paraconsistent program: da Costa's theory of inconsistent formal systems and Priest's logic of paradox, which admitted true contradictions without triviality, with Dummett's elements of intuitionism and Chagrov and Zakharyaschev's modal logic as the traditions' mature syntheses. The synthesis is organized around three themes: the constructivist program, in which meaning is use and proof---logic tied to mathematical practice; the modal and relevance programs, in which necessity, obligation, and consequence were made exact; and the paraconsistent program, in which inconsistency was domesticated rather than exorcised. It is concluded that the non-classical logics did not dethrone the classical but pluralized it---each logic a geometry of consequence fitted to a domain---and that the century from Brouwer to Priest is the finest demonstration that logic, examined, is mathematics' most revisable science.

title: Algorithmic Uncertainty Quantification via Process Noise Modeling
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to uncertainty quantification in machine learning by explicitly modeling process noise. Traditional methods often treat noise as an undesirable artifact, leading to potentially inaccurate confidence estimates. Our framework leverages stochastic differential equations (SDEs) – process noise models – directly integrated into the training process. These SDEs capture the inherent uncertainty in the data generation process, influencing the algorithm's confidence estimations in a more realistic and robust manner. We propose a methodology where the model parameters are learned alongside the primary machine learning model, effectively allowing the algorithm to adapt to the specific noise characteristics of the data. The core claim is that incorporating process noise modeling significantly improves machine learning algorithm performance, particularly in scenarios where data distributions are inherently uncertain. This represents a shift from viewing noise as an error to recognizing it as a fundamental component of the data, offering a more accurate and robust approach to uncertainty quantification.

title: Quantum Bias Field Modulation via Spacetime Geometry
abstract: Quantum bias field modulation, a concept previously relegated to theoretical exploration, presents a novel approach to manipulating quantum entanglement by shaping spacetime geometry. This paper explores the potential of utilizing precisely controlled gravitational fields to introduce subtle biases in the entanglement process, leading to enhanced correlations and enabling entirely new measurement outcomes. The core mechanism centers around the curvature of spacetime, offering a fundamentally different pathway compared to traditional entanglement manipulation techniques. We present a preliminary framework demonstrating the feasibility of this approach through mathematical modeling and simulation, highlighting the key challenges and potential breakthroughs in this emerging field.

title: Hybrid Intermediate-Task Training for Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Performance on XTREME-R
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: Can hybrid intermediate-task training (combining tasks of varying difficulty levels) improve zero-shot cross-lingual performance on XTREME-R compared to single-task training, as measured by XLM-R accuracy scores? title: 基于可扩展物理定律的通用人工智能架构
abstract: This paper proposes a novel architecture for General Artificial Intelligence (GAI) grounded in the principles of scalable physical laws. The core claim is that a GAI system can achieve continuous development and evolution by leveraging fundamental physical concepts. This approach moves beyond traditional artificial intelligence paradigms by incorporating self-organization, adaptation, and learning mechanisms, all rooted in physical laws. The proposed architecture utilizes a layered approach, beginning with a fundamental substrate governed by emergent physical processes, progressing through increasingly complex computational levels driven by physical constraints, and culminating in a generalized intelligence capable of abstract reasoning and problem-solving. Mathematical formulations are presented to illustrate key concepts and operational principles. The paper argues that this methodology offers a pathway to overcoming current limitations in AI development, fostering a truly adaptive and evolving intelligence. The central mechanism is the translation of physical laws into algorithmic structures, allowing the system to learn and refine its behavior in response to its environment and internal states. Ultimately, this research aims to establish a robust and scalable framework for GAI, enabling intelligent systems to continuously improve and adapt over time.

title: Quantum Error Correcting Neural Networks (QENN)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel architecture, the Quantum Error Correcting Neural Network (QENN), which leverages quantum error correction techniques to construct a fault-tolerant neural network. The core concept involves integrating classical neural networks with quantum error correction codes, such as the Quantum Capacity Decoding Error (QCDE), to mitigate the detrimental effects of quantum decoherence on neural network performance. Each neuron within the QENN utilizes a quantum bit (qubit) to represent its state, enabling the application of quantum error correction codes to detect and correct errors introduced by environmental noise. This approach aims to enhance the scalability and resilience of neural networks, potentially surpassing the capabilities of conventional neural networks in complex computational tasks. The paper details the theoretical framework, explores the integration of QCDE, and outlines a potential architecture for QENNs, focusing on the fundamental principles of combining classical and quantum computation for enhanced neural network functionality. The primary goal is to demonstrate the feasibility and advantages of utilizing quantum error correction within a neural network paradigm.

title: Quantum State Entropy Measurement for Quantum Sensors
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum state entropy measurement to enhance the performance of quantum sensors. Traditional sensing techniques often struggle with the detection of extremely weak signals due to limitations in signal-to-noise ratios. Quantum sensors, leveraging the principles of quantum mechanics, offer the potential for significantly improved sensitivity. However, accurately characterizing the state of the sensor and extracting information from it remains a challenge. Quantum state entropy measurement provides a powerful tool to address this issue by quantifying the uncertainty associated with the sensor's quantum state. This work details the theoretical framework, explores the mathematical underpinnings, and proposes a methodology for utilizing quantum state entropy measurement to improve the precision and sensitivity of quantum sensors. Specifically, we examine the relationship between entropy, sensor state, and the detected signal, outlining a strategy for extracting subtle changes related to the target signal. The core claim of this research is the successful implementation of quantum state entropy measurement for the precise detection of weak signals. ---

title: Dynamic Parameter Adjustment of Quantum Entanglement-Based Computation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel computational approach utilizing dynamic parameter adjustment based on quantum entanglement. Traditional computational methods are often static, leading to potential errors. This work proposes a method that leverages quantum entanglement to automatically adjust calculation parameters, thereby enhancing computational efficiency. The core mechanism involves exploiting the correlated states of entangled particles to dynamically modify the computation's trajectory, mitigating the effects of inherent errors. This innovation offers a significant advancement in computational performance compared to existing static methods.

title: Intent-to-Income: A Reference Decision Architecture for AI-first Decision Intelligence
abstract: AI-mediated search, commerce, and decision-support systems are often evaluated through behavioral or business outcomes such as interaction, engagement, and conversion, which do not necessarily represent the quality of the underlying user decision process. This paper proposes Intent-to-Income, a proprietary Reference Decision Architecture for AI-first Decision Intelligence focused on Customer Decisions and Commerce Decisions. The architecture defines a canonical core flow—Decision Signals → Decision Need → Decision Support → Decision Quality → Measurable Outcomes—and treats Decision Context as a cross-cutting layer. It is organized around four core components: Decision Journey Mapping, Decision Signal Matrix, Decision Interface, and Measurement Logic. Decision Quality is explicitly separated from terminal outcomes and is represented through three proposed dimensions: Understanding, Confidence, and Readiness. These dimensions are conceptual and have not yet been empirically validated. The paper also distinguishes Intent-to-Income from sales funnels, SEO frameworks, conversion-rate optimization frameworks, revenue attribution models, and product recommendation algorithms, while abstracting proprietary implementation details such as internal weighting and evaluation rules. The contribution is a decision-centered architecture that organizes Decision Signals, Decision Need, Decision Support, Decision Quality, and Measurable Outcomes into a connected structure for AI-mediated Customer and Commerce Decisions. Limitations and directions for empirical validation, measurement development, comparative evaluation, and human oversight are identified.

title: SegTSim: A Big Data Driven Segmented Temporal Simulation Framework for Heterogeneous Multivariate Systems
abstract: Heterogeneous multivariate time-series systems exhibit segment-specific nonlinear dynamics that challenge monolithic forecasting architectures. We propose SegTSim, a big-data-driven segmented temporal simulation framework that integrates segment-specific elasticity modeling with adaptive min-gating, dynamic production relocation optimization, multi-factor data fusion with exchange-rate propagation, and a deep ensemble validation pipeline. The framework is validated on US--Japan automotive trade data from USITC repositories spanning 2015 to 2025, comprising approximately 13000 annual records. Under a 25% perturbation scenario, Japanese import volume declines by 20.4% to 0.93 billion USD, while all output variables maintain coefficients of variation below 3.5% across 1000 ensemble inference runs.
