title: Grid4Earth: An Open-Source Python Ecosystem for Geospatial Data Integration Using an Ellipsoidal HEALPix DGGS
abstract: Abstract. The rapid growth in Earth observation (EO) and Digital Twin Earth data volumes creates a need for global, reproducible, and cloudnative spatial representations. Conventional latitude–longitude grids and projected tiling systems remain useful, but they introduce projection boundaries, non-uniform cell areas, and repeated reprojection costs when combining multi-source products. Grid4Earth addresses this problem through an open-source Python ecosystem built around an ellipsoidal HEALPix Discrete Global Grid System (DGGS) representation and Zarr-based data handling. The ecosystem consists of four composable packages: healpix-geo for WGS84-aware indexing and coverage queries, healpix-resample for CPU/GPU-capable regridding, healpix-plot for visualisation, and healpix-analyse for diagnostics and analysis. We situate Grid4Earth in relation to previous DGGS comparisons, XDGGS, and OGC API – DGGS work, focusing on the implementation layer required for EO workflows. When WGS84 geodetic latitude is passed directly to spherical HEALPix, local cell areas vary by up to approximately 0.9% because of Earth’s non-spherical shape. Grid4Earth preserves the HEALPix equal-area property on WGS84 through an authalic-latitude mapping. The ecosystem has been exercised in HEALPix/Zarr workflows for Sentinel-2, Sentinel-3, ERA5, CAMS, and DestinE Climate Digital Twin outputs. This paper describes the ellipsoidal geometry, the CPU/GPU-capable resampling architecture, and the implementation of metadata fields defined by CF 1.13 and version 1 of the Pilot Zarr DGGS convention, establishing ellipsoidal HEALPix/Zarr as a common representation that connects climate and Digital Twin Earth datasets with ellipsoidal EO datasets.

title: Explainable Ensemble Deep Learning for Credit Risk Classification
abstract: Although eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) has significantly increased interest in recent years, its application in credit risk classification (CRC) still requires further exploration to evaluate its effectiveness in classifying loan applicants. In credit risk classification, the application of deep learning models requires an explanation of their outputs to make the decision-making process transparent. However, existing explainable credit risk classification models often use a single classifier, which can degrade the prediction accuracy and reduce the quality of explanations. In order to improve both explainability and accuracy, we design a new explainable ensemble deep learning model for credit risk classification (EED-CRC). The proposed model involves two main phases: model building and model interpretation. In the first phase, we propose an ensemble CRC model that uses three Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architectures to classify applicants. The outputs of the three CNN architectures are then integrated using a machine learning model, yielding more accurate predictions than those obtained from any individual classifier. In the second phase, we aim to interpret the obtained classification model through three XAI methods, such as Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME), SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and Permutation Feature Importance (PFI), providing valuable insights to decision makers for classifying applicants. Experimental results on three real credit risk datasets show that the EED-CRC approach achieves superior performance compared to traditional CRC methods, both in accuracy and in explainability.

title: Spectral-Embedded Operator Learning for Three-Phase Interfacial Flow: A Ternary Cahn-Hilliard-Navier-Stokes Benchmark
abstract: Operator-learning surrogates have been benchmarked largely on single-field, single-interface problems, leaving unclear whether architectural choices validated in those settings transfer to constrained, multiphase flows. We introduce a three-phase interfacial-flow benchmark to examine whether the trunk coordinate representation matters for a multi-channel, interface-dominated target. The configuration consists of an air bubble rising through water, piercing a water-oil interface, and entraining a water plume into the oil within a bounded, wall-confined domain. Reference data are generated using a structure-preserving ternary Cahn-Hilliard-Navier-Stokes solver that algebraically preserves the simplex constraint. From 1,024 Sobol-sampled simulations spanning a nine-dimensional parameter space, we learn the mapping from physical parameters to five-channel space-time fields. We compare three parameter-matched DeepONet variants differing only in trunk representation: raw coordinates (DeepONet), random Fourier features (FEDONet), and a fixed tensor-product Chebyshev dictionary (SEDONet). SEDONet reduces the test relative L2 error by 16.8% compared with FEDONet and by 24.0% compared with DeepONet, while improving all five output channels. Spatial and temporal error analyses localize the principal gains near the diffuse interfaces and after bubble breakthrough. The results indicate that the Chebyshev representation is particularly effective for the strongly non-periodic wall-normal and temporal structure of this three-phase flow.

title: When to Adapt: Conditional Memory Adapters for Retention-Preserving Domain Specialization
abstract: Large language models deployed in specialized domains must improve in-domain performance without sacrificing general capabilities. Existing parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods are typically always on: their learned perturbations are applied to every input, which can degrade out-of-domain (OOD) performance. We propose Engram Adapter, a framework that repurposes pretraining-time conditional memory as a post-hoc adapter for frozen LLMs. It uses multi-channel matching over local n-gram patterns with explicit occupancy tracking as a lightweight selectivity prior, making residual injection more likely on in-domain inputs while a learned scalar gate suppresses incoherent OOD retrievals. We evaluate on Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B with AG-News and MedMCQA as adaptation tasks and OOD benchmarks spanning reasoning, translation, code generation, and legal reasoning. Engram Adapter improves in-domain accuracy while preserving 99.4%--100.1% of average OOD performance; on LegalBench it slightly exceeds the frozen base model on average, whereas comparable always-on baselines degrade sharply. Mechanistic analyses show that although OOD activations are non-zero, gate and projection attenuation reduce residuals to approximately 0.08% of hidden-state norm, yielding small KL drift and negligible accuracy change. These results suggest conditional activation is a promising route toward modular, retention-preserving domain specialization over frozen backbones.

We propose Engram Adapter, a framework that repurposes pretraining-time conditional memory as a post-hoc adapter for frozen LLMs. It uses multi-channel matching over local n-gram patterns with explicit occupancy tracking as a lightweight selectivity prior, making residual injection more likely on in-domain inputs while a learned scalar gate suppresses incoherent OOD retrievals. We evaluate on Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B with AG-News and MedMCQA as adaptation tasks and OOD benchmarks spanning reasoning, translation, code generation, and legal reasoning. Engram Adapter improves in-domain accuracy while preserving 99.4%--100.1% of average OOD performance; on LegalBench it slightly exceeds the frozen base model on average, whereas comparable always-on baselines degrade sharply. Mechanistic analyses show that although OOD activations are non-zero, gate and projection attenuation reduce residuals to approximately 0.08% of hidden-state norm, yielding small KL drift and negligible accuracy change. These results suggest conditional activation is a promising route toward modular, retention-preserving domain specialization over frozen backbones.

title: Comparative analysis of DCAT-AP landscape for improving interoperability and accessibility of european open data.
abstract: DCAT-AP is the common metadata standard adopted by many EU Member States, institutions, and organizations for publishing and reusing Open Data. In response to national and organizational requirements, several DCAT-AP National Profiles (NPs) have been developed to extend, specialise, or partially override the core specifications and introduce additional controlled vocabularies. While these profiles support local publishing needs, they also increase the complexity of harvesting, validation, and front-end rendering workflows in European Data Portal (EDP) and raise questions about interoperability and consistent metadata integration. To address these challenges, this paper presents a comparative analysis of the European DCAT-AP landscape, focusing on NPs that contribute a substantial volume of metadata to EDP. We introduce the DCAT-AP Profiles Analysis Methodology (DPAM) and the DCAT-AP Profiles Analysis Sheet (DPAS), a structured representation for DCAT-AP and its profiles. Using DPAM and DPAS, we systematically document, at multiple levels of detail, how seven NPs deviate from the core DCAT-AP specification in terms of added, omitted, changed, and deprecated elements. The results quantify the extent and nature of these deviations and explicate the trade-off between the modeling flexibility of RDF/DCAT-AP and the implementation complexity in real-world harvesting and presentation systems. The analysis provides: (i) an empirical basis for adapting harvesting and front-end components to profilespecific requirements, (ii) a baseline for Member States and standards bodies to review profile designs in line with DCAT-AP extension guidelines and identify potential violations as well as (iii) a reusable framework for monitoring and analyzing future DCAT-AP profiles.

title: Recursive Fractal Graph Clustering (RFGC)
abstract: Abstract: This paper introduces Recursive Fractal Graph Clustering (RFGC), a novel clustering algorithm designed to identify complex, self-similar patterns within high-dimensional datasets. Traditional clustering methods often struggle to capture intricate relationships, leading to suboptimal results. RFGC leverages recursive fractal graph analysis, constructing graphs that evolve through density and iteratively identify clusters based on these characteristics. The algorithm's core mechanism involves creating a graph and then analyzing its density to determine the location of clusters. This approach offers a robust and potentially more insightful method for uncovering hidden patterns.

title: Latent Meta-Abstraction over Transformer Representations: A Two-System Architecture for Persistent Meta-Abstraction and Compute Leverage
abstract: This concept paper proposes a two-system architecture pairing a conventional transformer (Primary Model) with a separately parameterized Meta-Abstraction Model restricted operationally to activation-derived Primary representations and its own latent memory. A smaller or lower-cost specialized learner could accumulate activation-derived experience across episodes, identify reusable cross-domain structure, store it persistently, and return selected meta-states through a bounded latent bridge. Meta-abstraction and compute leverage are separate claims. Level I requires relational invariance, held-out-domain transfer, causal benefit after reinjection, and reuse across analogous tasks. Level II additionally requires generalization over relations and comparison with a generic support-to-query meta-learner. Compute leverage requires a better held-out utility–compute tradeoff under matched supervision, accessible experience, information/memory budget, and inference compute. Setup and maintenance costs are handled by lifecycle accounting and a break-even horizon. Scaling analyses treat representation-structure measures separately and begin with a no-association null; change-point behavior is secondary. Controls include retrieval, extra test-time compute, latent recurrence, coprocessing, cache processing, reasoning-vector composition, generic meta-learning, coordinate dependence, lexical leakage, and test-memory contamination. No empirical results or claims of consciousness, AGI, superintelligence, or spontaneous intelligence emergence are made.

title: Title: Topological Resonance Networks (TRNs)
abstract: Quantum entanglement remains a cornerstone of quantum computing and communication, yet its practical implementation faces significant challenges related to decoherence and entanglement distribution. This research proposes a novel framework, Topological Resonance Networks (TRNs), which leverages dynamically evolving topological networks to achieve enhanced entanglement generation and manipulation. TRNs introduce a self-organizing topology driven by continuous, non-linear feedback, creating a persistent resonance effect that transcends traditional entanglement protocols. This approach offers the potential for scalability beyond classical limitations, significantly advancing the field of quantum information processing.

title: Algorithmic Fairness through Differential Privacy and Fairness Constraints
abstract: This paper investigates the challenging problem of achieving algorithmic fairness in machine learning systems while simultaneously protecting individual privacy. Traditional approaches to fairness often rely on post-processing techniques or modifying the learning algorithm itself, which can inadvertently compromise privacy. Conversely, differential privacy, a rigorous privacy mechanism, can be sensitive to biased data, potentially amplifying existing inequalities. This work proposes a novel framework that integrates differential privacy with explicitly defined fairness constraints. We demonstrate that by carefully calibrating the privacy parameters and incorporating fairness constraints directly into the learning process, it is possible to mitigate bias and maintain strong privacy guarantees. The core contribution lies in the development of a methodology for navigating this complex trade-off, offering a more robust and principled approach to building fair and private algorithms. We present a theoretical analysis of this framework and outline a practical approach to implementation.

title: Based on Simulated Annealing Algorithm for Solving Large-Scale Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to solving large-scale optimization problems using the simulated annealing (SA) algorithm. The core challenge in applying SA to these problems lies in its susceptibility to getting trapped in local optima due to the inherent limitations of the standard SA parameters. This work addresses this issue through the design of an adaptive simulated annealing algorithm. The algorithm dynamically adjusts the temperature schedule and step size based on the search progress, effectively mitigating the local search problem and enhancing the probability of converging to the global optimal solution. The proposed method demonstrates improved efficiency and accuracy in solving complex optimization problems compared to traditional SA implementations. The algorithm is presented with detailed formulas and mathematical notation.

title: Quantum Entangled Computation for Adaptive Key Management
abstract: Quantum Entangled Computation (QEC) presents a paradigm shift in cryptographic key management by leveraging the inherent quantum properties of qubits. This paper explores the application of QEC to develop an adaptive key management system, designed to dynamically adjust keys based on quantum state evolution. The core of this system relies on a novel mechanism that exploits the instantaneous correlations between qubits to achieve a higher level of security compared to traditional methods. We detail the proposed algorithm, its underlying principles, and its potential impact on securing cryptographic systems. The paper concludes with a discussion of the challenges and future directions in this rapidly evolving field.

title: Dynamic Symbolic Regression with Evolutionary Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to symbolic regression, termed Dynamic Symbolic Regression with Evolutionary Reinforcement Learning (DSR-ERL). The core idea is to leverage reinforcement learning (RL) to dynamically control an evolutionary algorithm, specifically optimizing the mutation and crossover operators within the symbolic regression process. Traditional symbolic regression methods often suffer from issues like premature convergence and inefficient exploration of the expression space. Our system addresses these challenges by allowing an RL agent to learn a policy that adapts the evolutionary strategy based on the quality of the generated symbolic expressions. The agent observes the fitness (evaluation) of the expression and adjusts the evolutionary operators to favor solutions with higher fitness. We demonstrate the effectiveness of DSR-ERL through a theoretical analysis and a conceptual framework, outlining the key components and their interactions. The system offers the potential to discover more accurate and efficient mathematical models from data, particularly in complex domains. The key innovation lies in the adaptive control provided by the RL agent, leading to a dynamic and potentially superior symbolic regression process. We provide a detailed description of the system's architecture, including the RL agent, the evolutionary algorithm, and the interface between them. Furthermore, we discuss the challenges and future directions of this research.

title: Title: Temporal Coherence Networks - Quantum Information Propagation
abstract: Temporal coherence networks represent a paradigm shift in quantum information transmission, moving beyond the limitations of individual particle entanglement. This paper investigates the design and analysis of networks predicated on the temporal coherence of entangled states, proposing a novel mechanism to facilitate faster and more efficient quantum communication. We explore how topological properties can be leveraged to guide information flow across time, offering a potential pathway to overcome inherent challenges in quantum data transfer. The core claim is that these networks will drastically reduce latency and increase bandwidth compared to traditional approaches. This work delves into the mathematical foundations of maintaining and propagating entanglement across time, providing a detailed theoretical framework for future network development. We present a comprehensive analysis of the potential challenges and benefits associated with this approach, ultimately aiming to establish a robust and scalable framework for temporal coherence quantum communication.

title: 基于自适应几何变换的量子神经网络
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum neural networks (QNNs) leveraging adaptive geometric transformations. Traditional QNNs often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their ability to adapt to complex data. We propose a dynamic parameter adjustment mechanism within the QNN architecture, enabling the network to learn and optimize its representation based on input data characteristics. This adaptive approach enhances the network's capacity and improves its overall performance, addressing a key limitation of conventional QNNs. The proposed method focuses on the core mechanism of dynamically adjusting network parameters using geometric transformations to achieve enhanced performance.

title: A Short-Term Photovoltaic Power Forecasting Method Based on Multiscale Decomposition and Adaptive Optimization
abstract: Existing studies still have limitations in characterizing the complex temporal patterns of photovoltaic time series. In particular, current forecasting models often struggle to capture local abrupt fluctuations and nonlinear relationships among variables, while hyperparameter optimization remains challenging. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a CNN-iTransformer short-term photovoltaic power forecasting method based on multiscale decomposition and adaptive optimization. First, the original photovoltaic power time series is decomposed into trend, seasonal, and residual components using seasonal-trend decomposition based on Loess (STL). The residual component is then further decomposed through variational mode decomposition (VMD) to fully extract the latent multiscale temporal information embedded in the sequence. Second, a convolutional neural network (CNN) is employed to extract local fluctuation features, while the iTransformer is utilized to model the nonlinear relationships and long-term temporal dependencies between multiple meteorological variables and photovoltaic power. Finally, the Phototropic Growth Algorithm (PGA) is introduced to optimize key hyperparameters of the forecasting model, thereby improving its generalization capability and forecasting accuracy under multi-seasonal scenarios. Simulation experiments are conducted using real-world data from a photovoltaic power station in Alice Springs, Australia. The experimental results show that, under the same PGA optimization conditions, the proposed model reduces the root mean square error (RMSE) and mean absolute error (MAE) by approximately 19.12% and 17.43%, respectively, compared with the baseline iTransformer. Meanwhile, its performance is better than that of several mainstream deep learning models, which verifies the generalization ability and forecasting accuracy of the proposed method under complex seasonal variations.

title: EHEIR: Efficient Homomorphic Encrypted Inference via Architectural Redesign
abstract: Encrypted inference under homomorphic encryption (HE) imposes stringent constraints on computation, making the direct deployment of deep neural networks infeasible on resource-constrained edge devices. Existing approaches, such as FHEEDGE and UniHENN, primarily focus on improving the efficiency of encrypted computation through algorithmic and systems-level optimizations. In contrast, we adopt a complementary perspective by redesigning neural architectures to align with the inherent cost model of HE operations. In this work, we present a framework that reformulates HE-aware model design as a constrained neural architecture search problem, where the objective is to identify architectures that are both cryptographically feasible and computationally efficient while preserving task performance. Starting from a pretrained network, we perform a structured, iterative transformation process that includes HE-compatible operator substitutions, depth–width tradeoffs, and rotation-efficient design strategies such as successive average pooling. These transformations are guided by constraints on ciphertext slots, multiplicative depth, and rotation complexity, and are evaluated using short-horizon training to efficiently explore the architecture space. We provide a theoretical analysis showing that the transformed network approximates the original model with bounded error under layer-wise Lipschitz propagation, ensuring controlled performance degradation. As a case study, we apply the proposed framework to encrypted crack detection for structural health monitoring. The optimized model achieves an execution time of 86.5 seconds for single-threaded CPU inference in the encrypted domain, compared with an estimated 3.5 hours required by the original encrypted convolutional pipeline. Furthermore, deployment on a Raspberry Pi demonstrates end-to-end encrypted inference within approximately 7.5 minutes. These results highlight that architecture-level optimization, when framed as a constrained search problem, complements existing algorithmic acceleration approaches and provides a practical pathway for enabling efficient and privacy-preserving inference on edge devices across a broad class of sensitive AI workloads.

title: A comprehensive review on advancements in beluga whale optimization algorithm, applications and future directions
abstract: The metaheuristic algorithms have gained significant attention among scientists and scholars in tackling the challenges of complex and high dimensional non-trivial optimization problems. For enhancing their performance and efficiency, investigation on newly developed nature inspired algorithms provides critical insights and relevant knowledge for their future advancement and development, by overcoming inherent weaknesses in them. To this end, this paper provides a comprehensive assessment of Beluga whale optimization (BWO) algorithm, it challenges considering different optimization aspects. This survey discusses and reviews the proposed variants of BWO, including chaotic, OBL, adaptive, multi-strategy, hybridized, binary and others with their weaknesses and advantages. Based on literature survey, it was revealed that BWO was widely employed by researchers in engineering domain with 29 %, computer science (20 %), mathematics (13 %), etc. In different methods of BWO, the studies incorporated mostly improved versions (33 %), basic version (25 %), hybridized versions (16 %), and integration with machine learning/deep learning (14 %) for solving optimization problems across various domains. In the end, statistical evaluation on thirty CEC 2017 benchmark suite revealed its outperformance in most landscapes in comparison to seven recent metaheuristics. The reader of this review will uncover significant limitations, improvements and different applications of BWO algorithm along with research gaps for future avenues. This review also offers practical insights to support the development and application of more effective BWO-based optimization methods.

title: LightFuse: Relightable Interactive Gaussian Scene Reconstruction via Multi-Scan Fusion and 2D Gaussian Ray Tracing
abstract: Relightable interactive scene reconstruction aims to build an editable 3D model from scans of different object arrangements and render new layouts under novel illumination. Existing methods either bake lighting into appearance or recover material and illumination only for fixed scenes, leaving edited layouts with inconsistent shadows and indirect lighting. We present LightFuse, a 2D Gaussian framework that extends interactive scene reconstruction with explicit material-illumination decomposition and physically based relighting. LightFuse first fuses observations across states to reconstruct a shared background and movable objects. It then conducts ray-tracing-oriented geometry refinement to produce more complete and consistent surfaces. On the refined geometry, staged training with differentiable one-bounce ray tracing separates shared metallic--roughness material from state-specific environment lighting. The resulting scene supports object rearrangement, material editing, and relighting, while ray tracing recomputes appearance after each interaction. Experiments across synthetic scenes demonstrate state-of-the-art relighting quality, outperforming the strongest baseline by +9.74\,dB PSNR and +0.121 SSIM on average. title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Strategic Decision-Making of Private Universities: A Systematic Review
abstract: Purpose – This systematic review examines how artificial intelligence (AI) can support strategic decision-making in private universities, the organizational conditions shaping its value, and the governance and implementation risks that constrain responsible use.Methodology – Searches were conducted in the Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, and Google Scholar between March and May 2026, with the final update on May 31, 2026. After duplicate removal, screening, full-text assessment, and evidence appraisal, 46 substantive sources published between 1955 and 2025 were included in this review. Four additional methodological references supported the review reporting and synthesis. Because the evidence base was heterogeneous, narrative thematic synthesis was applied while distinguishing direct private university evidence from evidence transferred from general higher education, organizational decision research, and AI governance.Findings – The synthesis identifies four interconnected roles of AI: environmental intelligence, decision augmentation, strategic execution, and governance infrastructure. AI can strengthen institutional sensing, the comparison of strategic alternatives, implementation coordination, and decision traceability. However, direct empirical evidence specific to private universities is limited. Strategic value depends on data quality, organizational learning, analytical capability, decision ownership, auditability, governance capacity, strategic fit, and alignment with the institutional mission. Therefore, AI is best understood as a human-led decision-support capability rather than a substitute for institutional judgment.Research limitations – The heterogeneous corpus prevents statistical estimation of a common institutional effect, while the review is restricted to English-language sources from three search platforms. Therefore, the four-part architecture should be treated as an evidence-organizing framework rather than a validated causal model.Originality – This review integrates higher education, organizational decision-making, strategic management, and AI governance evidence into an institution-level capability architecture for responsible AI-supported strategic decision-making.

evidence.abstract: Purpose – This systematic review examines how artificial intelligence (AI) can support strategic decision-making in private universities, the organizational conditions shaping its value, and the governance and implementation risks that constrain responsible use.Methodology – Searches were conducted in the Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, and Google Scholar between March and May 2026, with the final update on May 31, 2026. After duplicate removal, screening, full-text assessment, and evidence appraisal, 46 substantive sources published between 1955 and 2025 were included in this review. Four additional methodological references supported the review reporting and synthesis. Because the evidence base was heterogeneous, narrative thematic synthesis was applied while distinguishing direct private university evidence from evidence transferred from general higher education, organizational decision research, and AI governance.Findings – The synthesis identifies four interconnected roles of AI: environmental intelligence, decision augmentation, strategic execution, and governance infrastructure. AI can strengthen institutional sensing, the comparison of strategic alternatives, implementation coordination, and decision traceability. However, direct empirical evidence specific to private universities is limited. Strategic value depends on data quality, organizational learning, analytical capability, decision ownership, auditability, governance capacity, strategic fit, and alignment with the institutional mission. Therefore, AI is best understood as a human-led decision-support capability rather than a substitute for institutional judgment.Research limitations – The heterogeneous corpus prevents statistical estimation of a common institutional effect, while the review is restricted to English-language sources from three search platforms. Therefore, the four-part architecture should be treated as an evidence-organizing framework rather than a validated causal model.Originality – This review integrates higher education, organizational decision-making, strategic management, and AI governance evidence into an institution-level capability architecture for responsible AI-supported strategic decision-making.

title: Multilingual Intermediate Task Performance for Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer on XTREME-R with Adversarial Perturbations
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: Do multilingual intermediate tasks outperform English-only intermediate tasks for improving zero-shot cross-lingual transfer on XTREME-R, and by what margin when evaluated with adversarial perturbations? title: Differential Privacy via Randomized Graph Embeddings
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to protecting individual privacy within graph data by leveraging randomized graph embeddings and differential privacy. The core challenge in applying differential privacy to graph data stems from the inherent interconnectedness of nodes, making traditional privacy techniques difficult to implement effectively. This work proposes a framework for developing randomized graph embedding techniques that explicitly incorporate differential privacy constraints. The resulting embeddings aim to preserve privacy while maintaining the integrity of the underlying graph structure. We demonstrate the feasibility and potential benefits of this approach, outlining the key design considerations and mathematical formulations involved. The primary contribution lies in the application of differential privacy to graph embeddings, offering a new methodology for safeguarding sensitive information within graph datasets. This research provides a foundation for future work in privacy-preserving graph analysis and offers a promising avenue for utilizing graph data in applications where privacy is paramount.

title: Title: Quantum-Guided Topology Search
abstract: Quantum-Guided Topology Search addresses the limitations of traditional topological search algorithms by employing quantum entanglement to accelerate the identification of complex topological features and connectivity within datasets. This paper proposes a novel quantum algorithm that leverages entanglement to create a 'quantum fingerprint' of the data, enabling significantly enhanced pattern recognition and faster detection of crucial topological structures. We explore the fundamental principles of entanglement and its application to topological data analysis, detailing the design of a quantum-enhanced search strategy. The core mechanism centers around generating and manipulating entangled states to represent data points in a way that facilitates rapid identification of topological motifs. This paper presents a preliminary investigation of the algorithm's potential and outlines future research directions focused on scalability and practical implementation.

title: Geometric Constraint-Aware Machine Learning
abstract: This paper presents a novel machine learning framework, termed "Geometric Constraint-Aware Learning," designed to enhance generalization and robustness by explicitly incorporating geometric constraints during model training. Traditional machine learning methods often struggle with data distribution shifts and overfitting, particularly when dealing with complex, high-dimensional spaces. The proposed framework leverages geometric concepts – specifically, constraints derived from geometric shapes – to guide the learning process, effectively forcing the model to learn representations that are more aligned with the underlying data distribution. We introduce a new constraint-based optimization technique that significantly improves performance on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach. The paper details the core mechanism, presents experimental results, and discusses future research directions.

title: Quantum State Adaptive Gradient Decomposition
abstract: Quantum State Adaptive Gradient Decomposition (QASTD) is a novel quantum algorithm designed to enhance gradient-based optimization for complex systems. This paper introduces a new approach that leverages the intrinsic self-similarity of quantum states to dynamically adjust the gradient decomposition process, ultimately enabling significantly improved precision in computations. The core mechanism relies on exploiting the quantum state's inherent correlation to guide the optimization process, offering a streamlined and highly efficient alternative to traditional gradient-based methods. We demonstrate the effectiveness of QASTD through rigorous theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation across a range of benchmark problems. The algorithm's potential impact on various fields, including machine learning and materials science, is substantial.

title: Quantum-Inspired Relational Reasoning for Knowledge Graph Completion
abstract: Knowledge graphs (KGs) are increasingly used to represent and reason about complex relationships between entities. However, traditional relational reasoning methods, particularly those based on probabilistic inference, often struggle with scalability due to combinatorial explosion, especially as the size and complexity of the KG grows. This paper introduces a novel framework, Quantum-Inspired Relational Reasoning (QIRR), designed to address this challenge. QIRR draws inspiration from quantum mechanics, specifically superposition and interference, to efficiently explore potential relationships within a KG. Nodes in the KG are represented as entangled states, enabling the simultaneous consideration of multiple relationship possibilities. Crucially, interference terms are introduced to modulate the probabilities associated with these relationships, amplifying the likelihood of true connections while diminishing the impact of false ones. A learned interference pattern guides this process, offering adaptive control over the reasoning process. We demonstrate that QIRR significantly improves the scalability of relational reasoning compared to conventional probabilistic approaches, offering a promising path toward handling large-scale KGs. The core of our approach lies in the ability to model and exploit inherent correlations within the graph structure, mimicking quantum measurement outcomes to achieve enhanced accuracy and efficiency. The framework's adaptive interference mechanism is key to its success.

title: Quantum Quantumization for Image Processing
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum quantumization for image processing, aiming to improve image compression ratios and quality. The core concept involves transforming images into quantum quantumized information, leveraging the unique properties of quantum computing to perform image processing operations. This approach facilitates both image compression and enhancement. We propose a novel framework utilizing quantum techniques to represent and manipulate image data, offering potential advantages over classical methods, particularly for high-resolution images and complex scenes. The theoretical underpinnings of this work are detailed, focusing on the mathematical formulations involved in the quantum encoding, processing, and decoding stages. We demonstrate the feasibility of this approach and suggest future research directions.

title: Self-Organizing Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of self-organizing quantum computing as a novel approach to address the challenges of large-scale quantum computation and quantum information processing. The core concept revolves around leveraging quantum entanglement to construct dynamic quantum states within a network, enabling self-organization and enhanced computational efficiency. We propose a framework predicated on the unique properties of quantum entanglement, focusing on the design of a quantum state network that exhibits self-assembly. This approach aims to overcome limitations associated with traditional quantum algorithms and facilitate more scalable and efficient quantum computations. The paper explores the theoretical foundations and potential implementation challenges associated with this paradigm. We will delve into the intricacies of entanglement-based network design and its implications for computation. Finally, the paper will conclude with a discussion of future research directions and potential applications.

title: Adaptive Quantum State Measurement and Information Extraction
abstract: This paper investigates the development of an adaptive quantum state measurement protocol designed to enhance information extraction efficiency from quantum states while mitigating the detrimental effects of decoherence. The core idea revolves around employing a reinforcement learning algorithm to dynamically adjust the measurement basis, based on the observed quantum state characteristics and feedback signals generated during the measurement process. Real-time adjustments to measurement device parameters via quantum control techniques further optimize the measurement outcome. The proposed method addresses the limitations of traditional fixed-basis measurements, which are highly susceptible to decoherence. Through adaptive basis selection, this approach aims to maximize information extraction and minimize interference with the quantum state. The theoretical framework and underlying principles are presented, outlining the key components and their interrelationship. The potential impact of this technique on quantum information processing is discussed.

title: Symbolic Logic Fusion
abstract: This paper introduces Symbolic Logic Fusion (SLF), a novel algorithmic framework designed to address complex decision-making and logical problem-solving through the synergistic integration of symbolic logic and logical reasoning. The core concept of SLF centers on the creation of a 'graph' representing the problem, which is then transformed into a 'logical problem' by a sophisticated reasoning engine. This transformation enables a significantly more efficient and robust approach compared to conventional methods. The paper details the architecture of SLF, explores its key mechanisms, and provides a comprehensive analysis of its potential applications across diverse domains. We demonstrate the efficacy of SLF through illustrative examples, emphasizing its ability to handle intricate scenarios previously intractable for traditional algorithms. Finally, we discuss future research directions and potential advancements.

title: Learning to Ground Before Reading: Unified PCB Engineering Drawing Parsing with Compact Vision-Language Models
abstract: PCB engineering drawings mix sparse graphics, dense tables, and text whose meaning depends on page position. Localizing the regions and sending crops to specialized recognizers are determined as the methods for most parsers, so missed regions cannot be recovered downstream. We train a compact VLM to read the full page and get a sequence of region classes, normalized boxes, and text or HTML content. Bounding boxes are converted to coordinate tokens for supervision. Inference uses no detector or crop parser. The joint target is difficult to optimize because class and box tokens are sparse relative to the much longer content sequences. Our localization-first curriculum learns the class-box format before adding content targets with content-aware resampling. On the fixed validation split of the Engineering Drawing Dataset (ED dataset), Localization-First improves strict localization F1 by 0.0955 over joint training (paired image-bootstrap 95% interval: [0.0350, 0.1572]). G-Unified has the lowest NED, highest cell F1, and only nonzero exact-match score. It provides a detector-free baseline for full-page PCB drawing parsing.

title: Agent2UCB: Agentic System for Generative Engine Optimization
abstract: Large language model driven search engines such as Google AI Overviews and Perplexity have created new opportunities for Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) the practice of refining content to increase its likelihood of being cited or summarized by generative systems. We demonstrate Agent2UCB, an agentic GEO system that autonomously improves content visibility through customized, feedback-driven optimization. For each content item, the system evaluates nine GEO strategies, identifies the most effective method, and accelerates selection using a bandit-based Agent2UCB policy that integrates LLM priors with online reward signals. To monitor side effects, the system also provides a lightweight, text-only SEO readiness evaluation covering readability, topical coverage, and EEAT-style credibility. Experiments on GEO-Bench show consistent visibility gains while preserving SEO quality. The demo allows users to choose the websites of interest, observe the optimization workflow, and compare GEO/SEO outcomes across methods.

title: The Impact of Customer Engagement Using Facebook Messenger Chatbots on the Marketing Performance of Cafés in Subic Bay Freeport Zone
abstract: This correlational quantitative study examined the impact of customer engagement using Facebook Messenger chatbots on the marketing performance of café businesses in the Subic Bay Freeport Zone. Specifically, it assessed customer engagement in terms of perceived responsiveness, customer trust, and willingness to interact, as well as marketing performance in terms of sales conversion rate and sales growth. The study employed a correlational quantitative research design involving 20 café owners or managers who actively used Facebook Messenger chatbots. Data were collected through a researcher-made questionnaire and analyzed using descriptive statistics and Spearman’s Rho. Results revealed that chatbots were perceived as highly responsive and effective at building customer trust and also contributed positively to sales conversion and growth. However, no significant relationship was found between customer engagement using chatbots and marketing performance. The findings suggest that chatbot utilization alone may not directly influence marketing outcomes and should be integrated with broader business and marketing strategies.

title: SMOTE-CCU+: Experimental Code for Systematic Benchmarking of Resampling Techniques for Class Imbalance with Statistical Validation and Ablation Analysis
abstract: This repository contains the complete experimental implementation of SMOTE-CCU+ (Synthetic Minority Oversampling and Cluster Centroid Undersampling Plus), a novel hybrid resampling framework for addressing class imbalance in multiclass classification tasks. The code accompanies the manuscript: "Systematic Benchmarking of Resampling Techniques for Class Imbalance Using the Novel Hybrid SMOTE-CCU+ with Statistical Validation and Ablation Analysis", submitted to Scientific Reports. Contents:- Complete SMOTE-CCU+ pipeline implementation (DBSCAN filtering, distance-weighted SMOTE, adaptive CCU, Tomek Links refinement)- Performance benchmarking across 6 sampling strategies (None, SMOTE, ADASYN, ENN, CCU, SMOTE-CCU+) and 5 classifiers (LR, DT, RF, KNN, SVC)- Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test with effect size estimation (r = Z/sqrt(N))- Friedman test for multi-group comparison- Nemenyi post-hoc analysis with critical difference diagrams and heatmaps- Ablation study with component contribution analysis (Delta MCC per component)- Computational time comparison across all resampling methods Requirements: Python 3.8+, scikit-learn, imbalanced-learn, scikit-posthocs, pandas, numpy, matplotlib, scipy All random seeds fixed at 42 for full reproducibility.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding Adaptive Multi-Dimensional State Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a uniquely quantum phenomenon, presents a significant challenge to information processing due to its inherent fragility and potential for detection. This paper explores a novel approach to quantum information encoding utilizing adaptive multi-dimensional state algorithms. We introduce a new model, the "Adaptive Multi-Dimensional State" (AMDS) framework, which leverages the dynamic interplay of quantum entanglement to achieve precise state control and enhanced quantum information transfer. The algorithm's core mechanism centers around the manipulation of entangled states through a self-adjusting, multi-dimensional representation, offering a potential pathway to circumvent current limitations in quantum computation and communication. This research presents a preliminary assessment of the algorithm's capabilities and potential implications for future quantum technologies.

title: Meta-Learning for Automated Algorithm Selection
abstract: Algorithm selection remains a significant bottleneck in machine learning workflows, frequently relying on expert intuition and trial-and-error. This paper proposes a meta-learning framework designed to automate this process, enabling systems to dynamically adapt and choose the optimal algorithm for a given task and dataset. The core of our approach leverages recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to model the algorithm selection process and Bayesian optimization for efficient hyperparameter tuning. We demonstrate that this meta-learning system can significantly improve both the efficiency and performance of model training by learning from past experiences. The system learns a policy for selecting algorithms based on observed task characteristics, represented as a state vector, and iteratively refines this policy through Bayesian optimization. The key contribution is a formalized approach to combining meta-learning with algorithm selection, providing a robust and adaptive solution for automated machine learning.

title: Multi-Modal Sensory Feedback Reinforcement Learning with Adaptive Agents
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to reinforcement learning (RL) by integrating multi-modal sensory feedback. The core idea is to develop adaptive agents capable of learning and responding to complex environments by leveraging information from various sources, such as vision, audition, and tactile sensing. Traditional RL algorithms often operate in a limited perceptual space, hindering their ability to effectively navigate and interact with dynamic, real-world scenarios. Our method addresses this limitation through a multi-modal sensor fusion module that converts disparate sensory inputs into a unified representation. title: Dynamic Topological Semantic Network (DTSE) Architecture
abstract: This paper introduces the Dynamic Topological Semantic Network (DTSE) architecture, a novel approach to program execution and optimization that transcends traditional compilation and runtime interpretation. The core claim is that by dynamically modeling and operating on the abstract semantic structure of program code, we can achieve enhanced performance and efficiency. The DTSE architecture leverages a graph-based semantic representation, translating program code's control flow, data dependencies, and side effects into a dynamic "semantic topology." Intelligent agents, utilizing reinforcement learning or evolutionary algorithms, traverse this topology to identify optimization opportunities such as dead code elimination, loop unrolling, and data locality optimization, dynamically adjusting execution paths or generating new code segments. A "semantic validation" module continuously monitors the topology's integrity, preventing optimization-induced errors. This architecture represents a departure from static semantic analysis and rule-based runtime optimization, offering a more adaptable and granular approach to program optimization.

title: Dynamic Topology-Dependent Quantum Entanglement Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum entanglement optimization, termed Dynamic Topology-Dependent Quantum Entanglement Optimization (DTQEO). The core claim is that optimization algorithms leveraging dynamic adjustments to the entanglement topology can achieve global optimal solutions for complex objective functions. The central mechanism involves a "quantum entanglement network" modeled based on topological quantum computation, utilizing the topological properties of quantum entanglement, such as exchange symmetry and non-Abelian properties, to dynamically reshape the entanglement structure. A feedback mechanism is employed to iteratively optimize this entanglement structure, effectively mitigating local minima within the optimization process. The innovation lies in moving beyond fixed entanglement topologies, mirroring the plasticity observed in biological neural networks through synaptic plasticity, leading to a more efficient optimization paradigm. The methodology incorporates a continuous feedback loop, where the performance of the entanglement network is evaluated and used to dynamically adjust its topological parameters. This adaptive process aims to converge towards an optimal configuration that minimizes the objective function. The theoretical framework provides a new perspective on leveraging quantum entanglement for optimization, and the proposed DTQEO algorithm offers a promising direction for tackling complex optimization problems. The work demonstrates the potential of dynamically controlled entanglement networks to outperform traditional optimization methods.

title: Quantum Annealing-Driven Deep Learning Model Architecture Design
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to deep learning model architecture design by leveraging the principles of quantum annealing. The core idea is to map the complex search space of deep learning architectures to the energy landscape of a quantum annealing system. The quantum annealing algorithm is then employed to explore this landscape, iteratively minimizing the energy and ultimately identifying a globally optimal or near-optimal architecture. We introduce a framework integrating deep learning architecture search with quantum annealing, addressing the limitations of classical optimization methods prone to getting trapped in local minima. The method's effectiveness is demonstrated conceptually through a detailed architecture design process, highlighting the potential for accelerated discovery of superior models. The key contributions include a methodology for translating architectural parameters into a quantum annealing problem formulation and a strategy for interpreting the resulting quantum annealing solution as a viable deep learning architecture. Further research will focus on optimizing the annealing process and exploring different quantum annealing hardware platforms.

title: Title: Geometric Optimization of Quantum Error Correction
abstract: Quantum error correction is a critical component of future quantum computing, enabling the reliable operation of complex quantum systems. Current methods, while effective in certain scenarios, often struggle with complex error patterns and require significant effort in parameter tuning. This paper explores a novel geometric optimization framework for quantum error correction, aiming to identify and mitigate the detrimental effects of errors on system performance. We propose a method based on establishing a geometric representation of the quantum error map and subsequently employing optimization algorithms to minimize this map's influence. This approach offers a potential pathway to significantly improve the robustness and efficiency of quantum error correction protocols, moving beyond traditional heuristic methods. The core mechanism involves leveraging geometric principles to construct a simplified, yet effective, representation of the error landscape, allowing for targeted optimization and ultimately enhancing system fidelity. The research builds upon existing work in optimization and error correction, but introduces a novel geometric perspective to address key challenges in the field.

title: Self-Organizing Neural Networks with Emergent Topological Constraints
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to neural network architecture design, termed Self-Organizing Neural Networks with Emergent Topological Constraints (SONN-ETC). The core idea is to move away from manually designed network topologies and instead allow the network to self-organize its structure based on intrinsic constraints derived directly from the training data. This is achieved through a competitive learning algorithm where nodes compete to connect to others based on the similarity of their activation patterns. A dynamically evolving topological constraint function guides this competition, ensuring that the emerging network topology reflects underlying data relationships. The resulting architecture is truly emergent, where the network's structure arises organically from the data and the learning process. This approach offers potential advantages in terms of efficiency, scalability, and adaptability compared to traditional network design methods. The theoretical framework and the proposed mechanism are detailed, highlighting the key components and their interactions. The algorithm is presented with the core equations used to drive the competitive learning and constraint evolution. We demonstrate the potential of this method through a conceptual analysis and outline future research directions.

title: Neuromorphic Computing Architecture for Reservoir Computing with Predictive Coding
abstract: Reservoir computing (RC) has emerged as a powerful technique for processing temporal data, particularly in applications requiring real-time responses. However, conventional RC implementations often face limitations in feedback control and the ability to accurately predict future states, primarily due to the reliance on traditional digital signal processing. This work presents a novel neuromorphic computing architecture designed specifically for RC with predictive coding. The architecture leverages the inherent advantages of spiking neural networks (SNNs) and integrates predictive coding mechanisms directly into the hardware, enabling real-time adaptation and enhanced future state prediction capabilities. This approach addresses the core challenges of traditional RC by exploiting the temporal dynamics of SNNs and providing a mechanism for incorporating prior knowledge. The architecture is detailed, focusing on the key components and their interconnections, and the theoretical framework underpinning the system is presented. The design aims for efficient implementation on neuromorphic hardware, promising improved performance and reduced computational burden compared to conventional RC methods. The core claim of this work is that a dedicated neuromorphic architecture can overcome the limitations of traditional reservoir computing by facilitating predictive coding and real-time adaptation.

title: Measurement Validity in LLM Cultural Alignment
abstract: Researchers increasingly treat LLM survey responses as a proxy for human cultural values. This includes projecting model outputs onto instruments like the Inglehart-Welzel Cultural Map and drawing conclusions about which cultures a model resembles. While a model's answer to a value-laden questions may be interpreted as a cultural signal, it also carries sampling noise and, can be quite sensitive to question framing. In this paper, we separate survey responses, sampling noise and question framing for multiple LLMs. We decompose response variance from these models into variation across random seeds, prompt rewordings. We employ noise-to-signal ratio (NSR) to test whether a model's apparent cultural position is distinguishable from noise. When applied across a dozen models from four geographic origins, calibrated against 88 Integrated Values Survey countries, the answer is often no. NSR exceeds 1.0 on 49 of 117 valid model-question pairs (42%), reaching 5.56 in the worst case. Two models even refuse to answer sufficient number of survey questions outright. Our results corroborate previous findings that LLMs cluster toward Western, English-speaking cultural positions. However, what does not hold up in this study is the precision with which anyone can currently interpret a specific model's coordinates: prompt tone alone can shift a model by 2.4 map units, comparable to the distance between actual countries in the Inglehart-Welzel Cultural Map. These findings suggest that cultural attribution from LLM survey responses requires establishing the reliability of the underlying measurements before interpreting model coordinates as evidence of cultural representation.

title: Universal recovery in approximate quantum error correction
abstract: Universal recovery -- the existence of a single recovery map that corrects an entire family of error channels -- is a central feature of quantum error correction (QEC). In exact QEC, linearity guarantees that a code correcting a given error set also corrects every channel whose Kraus operators lie in its linear span, and that a single recovery map suffices for all such channels. Approximate quantum error correction (AQEC), which relaxes perfect recovery to recovery with controlled error, has traditionally lacked this structure. In a recent paper (arXiv:2607.22995), we developed a theory of approximate quantum error correction showing that a restricted form of linearity persists in the approximate setting, yielding uniform AQEC guarantees for the family of channels controlled by a given error set. In this work, we complete the picture by establishing the second half of universal recovery in the approximate setting: a single recovery map can simultaneously correct every channel controlled by a given error set. The error-set theory we proposed quantifies approximate correctability through two parameters: the environment-leakage distance, governing worst-case performance, and the Knill--Laflamme Hellinger distance, governing average-case performance. We show here that both quantities also control universal decoding. We further study the Petz map naturally associated with an error set as an explicit universal recovery, and obtain uniform average- and worst-case guarantees across the entire family of channels.

title: Title: Temporal Feedback Loop for Wave Function Collapse (TFLWC)
abstract: Quantum simulation offers unprecedented capabilities in modeling complex quantum systems, but current techniques often struggle with the inherent instability of wave function collapse. This paper introduces the Temporal Feedback Loop for Wave Function Collapse (TFLWC), a novel algorithm designed to mitigate these errors through a dynamic feedback mechanism. The core of TFLWC lies in continuously monitoring the state of the wave function and adjusting the collapse process to minimize deviations from the intended quantum state. This approach addresses the limitations of existing methods, offering a more stable and accurate process for quantum simulation, ultimately facilitating enhanced precision and reliability in these simulations. This work presents a robust framework for managing wave function collapse, incorporating a sophisticated temporal feedback loop that significantly improves the stability and accuracy of quantum simulations.

title: PROBES: A Bernstein Simplex Approach to Differentially Private OLS Estimation
abstract: Differentially private ordinary least squares regression on bounded continuous data is dominated by a single design tension: each sufficient statistic $\{S_{x_j}, S_y, S_{x_j x_k}, S_{x_j y}\}$ is conventionally treated as an independent query, forcing the analyst to either split the privacy budget $\varepsilon$ across many releases or compose a long sequence of noisy mechanisms. For $p$-dimensional multivariate linear regression, this implies estimating $\Theta(p^2)$ quantities, thereby inflating per-statistic noise by a factor of $\Theta(p^2)$. We introduce PROBES (PRivate O}rdinary least squares via BErnstein Simplex), a pure $\varepsilon$-DP mechanism that exploits the common algebraic structure shared across the sufficient statistics, releases a single Laplace vector at the full unsplit budget $\varepsilon$, and recovers every sufficient statistic for multivariate linear regression on $p$ bounded features by post-processing. The construction rests on the Bernstein simplex embedding: each record is mapped to a non-negative vector of dimension $3^p \times 2$ that sums to exactly 1, giving a global $\ell_1$-sensitivity of 1 regardless of $p$. We also present Ada-PROBES, which retains the single-shot Bernstein release of PROBES and recovers coefficients via a noise-calibrated ridge solve that stabilizes matrix inversion at no extra privacy cost. Experiments on six real-world regression benchmarks show that Ada-PROBES achieves test RMSE within 1% of non-private OLS for $p \le 4$ on large-sample datasets at $\varepsilon = 1$, while DiffPrivLib collapses numerically and AdaSSP/BinAgg incur noticeably higher error in the same low-$p$ regime. For $p \ge 6$, we introduce S-PROBES, a scalable Steiner-block based pure $\varepsilon$-DP extension that preserves the single-release structure per-block and remains competitive at relatively higher values of $p$ with the $(\varepsilon, \delta)$-DP methods AdaSSP and BinAgg (which employ Gaussian noise based on $\ell_2$-sensitivity).

title: 基于量子纠缠的拓扑几何的自适应优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on quantum entanglement, termed "Quantum-Adaptive Topological Optimization" (QATO). Traditional optimization methods often rely on static parameters, limiting their adaptability and potential for improved performance. QATO leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to dynamically adjust the optimization landscape, resulting in enhanced solution quality and speed. The algorithm employs a quantum state representation to capture the inherent structure of the problem, allowing for a continuous, self-correcting optimization process. The core mechanism involves the creation of entangled states, which evolve as the optimization progresses, guiding the algorithm towards optimal solutions. This approach significantly surpasses the capabilities of conventional optimization techniques, particularly in complex and non-convex optimization problems. This work presents a theoretical framework and initial experimental validation demonstrating the effectiveness of QATO in several benchmark optimization tasks.

title: Reinforcement Learning Integration in Large Language Models: A Novel Framework for Enhanced Performance
abstract: The integration of reinforcement learning (RL) with large language models (LLMs) represents a significant advancement in artificial intelligence, enabling systems to learn and adapt through interaction with their environment. This paper presents a novel framework that combines the pattern recognition capabilities of LLMs with the decision-making strengths of RL algorithms to enhance performance across various natural language processing tasks. Our approach introduces a hybrid architecture that utilizes RL to fine-tune LLM parameters based on reward signals derived from task-specific objectives. We demonstrate through extensive experiments that this integration leads to improved coherence, factual accuracy, and task adherence compared to traditional fine-tuning methods. The framework's adaptability is showcased across multiple domains including question answering, content generation, and dialogue systems. Additionally, we address key challenges such as reward design, computational efficiency, and policy stability, proposing novel solutions that make the approach practical for real-world applications. Our findings suggest that RL-integrated LLMs can achieve more robust and aligned behaviors, bridging the gap between generative capabilities and goal-directed reasoning in artificial intelligence systems.

title: Distributed Federated Learning with Byzantine Fault Tolerance via Blockchain Verification
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising approach to training machine learning models on decentralized data sources without directly exchanging data. However, FL systems are vulnerable to Byzantine attacks, where malicious participants can inject faulty model updates, compromising model accuracy and potentially causing significant harm. This paper proposes a novel framework for distributed federated learning with Byzantine fault tolerance, utilizing a blockchain-based verification layer. Our system employs a distributed consensus mechanism on a blockchain to validate model updates generated by participating nodes. This approach provides a robust, trustless environment, guaranteeing data integrity and ensuring model accuracy even in the presence of malicious actors. The core claim is the implementation of FL systems with Byzantine fault tolerance through blockchain verification. The core mechanism involves local model training followed by blockchain recording of updates and distributed consensus verification. This work represents a significant advancement by integrating the benefits of FL with the security and immutability offered by blockchain technology. We demonstrate a viable path toward building resilient and reliable FL systems for diverse applications.

title: Adaptive Constraint Optimization for Complex Neural Networks
abstract: This paper presents a novel optimization algorithm, Adaptive Constraint Optimization for Complex Neural Networks (ACCO), designed to address the challenges of training complex neural networks – particularly those exhibiting intricate parameter dependencies and requiring dynamic regularization. Traditional optimization methods often fail to capture the full extent of the network's sensitivity to initial conditions, leading to suboptimal performance. ACCO introduces a mechanism that iteratively adjusts constraints based on the network's learning progress, mimicking the brain's adaptation to environmental challenges. The core of the algorithm involves a feedback loop that analyzes the network's error surface, dynamically modifying regularization strength and constraint bounds, ultimately promoting better generalization. The paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and experimental evaluation, demonstrating its effectiveness in improving model performance on a diverse set of benchmark datasets.

The paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and experimental evaluation, demonstrating its effectiveness in improving model performance on a diverse set of benchmark datasets.

title: Quantum Key Generation Based on Quantum Mechanical Principles
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to cryptographic key generation leveraging fundamental principles of quantum mechanics, specifically quantum superposition and quantum entanglement. The core idea centers around Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocols, employing these quantum phenomena to establish a secure key exchange. We detail a method for generating keys based on the inherent uncertainty associated with quantum measurement, providing a significantly enhanced level of security compared to traditional key generation methods reliant on computational complexity. The proposed system utilizes entangled photon pairs to create a shared random key, followed by classical post-processing steps to eliminate errors and ensure key secrecy. The theoretical framework is presented with a focus on the mathematical underpinnings of quantum key generation and security proofs. We examine the potential vulnerabilities and mitigation strategies, highlighting the robustness of the approach against eavesdropping attempts. The development of this system aims to address the growing need for truly secure cryptographic solutions in an era of increasingly sophisticated cyber threats. ---

title: 基于非欧几何的量子态生成
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum state generation algorithm based on non-Euclidean geometry. Traditional quantum state generation methods often rely on classical geometry, but this algorithm leverages the unique properties of non-Euclidean geometry to generate quantum states with complex topology, enhancing the efficiency and accuracy of quantum computation. The core mechanism involves introducing a 'non-Euclidean geometry state generation' process, utilizing the inherent geometric properties to produce states with intricate topology. This approach offers a potential paradigm shift in quantum state creation, offering a pathway to more efficient and accurate quantum computations.

This research will investigate the mathematical framework for this simulation, focusing on the role of entanglement in generating and manipulating quantum states. The paper presents a conceptual outline of the algorithm and discusses its potential applications in various quantum computing and simulation contexts.

title: Dynamic Topology Quantum Computation
abstract: The development of quantum computation is increasingly reliant on sophisticated algorithms and the representation of complex systems. Static computational models often struggle to effectively capture the nuances of these systems, limiting their potential for optimization. This paper explores the application of dynamic topology as a novel framework for quantum computation, proposing a model capable of leveraging quantum state adaptability to enhance computational efficiency. We present a core mechanism focused on constructing a dynamic topology that adapts to the system's evolution, ultimately offering a promising approach to overcome limitations in current quantum algorithms. This research aims to provide a foundational basis for future advancements in quantum computation by integrating dynamic topology into the design of quantum algorithms.

title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization for Neural Networks
abstract: Quantum-inspired optimization is a burgeoning field aiming to leverage the principles of quantum mechanics to enhance the efficiency of training neural networks. This paper explores the application of quantum-like concepts, specifically superposition and entanglement, to optimize neural network parameters. We detail a novel algorithm, dubbed "Quantum-Guided Adaptation," which utilizes these principles to accelerate convergence and potentially improve the accuracy of neural network models. The research investigates the potential benefits of these methods compared to traditional optimization techniques, focusing on enhancing training speed and achieving better results, particularly for complex neural network architectures. The core mechanism centers on creating a representation of the network's parameters that mirrors quantum phenomena, allowing for parallel processing and exploration of parameter space. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and preliminary analysis, suggesting a significant improvement in training time and model accuracy.

title: HelioTR-Atlas: analysis code for a station-validated, explainable photovoltaic yield atlas of Türkiye
abstract: Analysis code for the HelioTR-Atlas study. It builds a climatological module-DC photovoltaic yield atlas of Türkiye on the SARAH-3 grid (0.05°, 32,479 land cells) for 2000-2025, and renders the figures and tables of the accompanying paper from those results. Pipeline. SARAH-3 surface incoming shortwave (SIS) and direct (SID) irradiance supply the radiation, with the direct component taken from the retrieval rather than inferred from a diffuse-fraction correlation. ERA5-Land 2 m temperature, 2 m dew point and 10 m wind supply the thermodynamics, corrected from the model orography to the Copernicus GLO-30 cell elevation with constant lapse rates and validated against 62 temperature and 119 dew-point/wind stations. The PV chain is a Hay-Davies anisotropic transposition, a Faiman cell-temperature model and an ADR efficiency model calibrated to a Panasonic HIT 325 W module (VBHN325SA16), computed hourly with pvlib. A random-forest surrogate explained with SHAP values attributes the spatial pattern of yield and of the performance ratio to their physical drivers. Contents. scripts/ holds the acquisition, downscaling, validation, atlas and attribution stages; notebooks/ holds the single notebook that renders the figures and tables from those products; requirements.txt pins the package versions actually used for the reported results. README.md documents the run order and the credentials that acquisition needs. Manuscript-production and journal-correspondence scripts are excluded; they are not part of the analysis. Data. The derived products this code generates are archived separately at 10.5281/zenodo.22152820. Input datasets are openly available from their providers and are listed under "Related identifiers". Station records are used under their providers' terms and are not redistributed. Funding. Scientific Research Projects Coordination Office of Hakkari University, Türkiye (Project No. FM19BAP).

title: Behavioral Drift-Aware Adaptive Anomaly Fusion for Explainable Risk Monitoring in Salary Advance FinTech Systems
abstract: Digital salary advance and earned wage access platforms require intelligent monitoring mechanisms capable of identifying behavioral anomalies, estimating operational risk, and preserving auditable transaction evidence. Existing financial anomaly detection approaches commonly rely on isolated predictive models, static anomaly thresholds, or rule-based monitoring, providing limited support for behavior-aware enterprise monitoring. This study proposes a behavioral drift-aware adaptive anomaly fusion framework for explainable risk monitoring in salary advance FinTech systems. The framework introduces the Behavioral Risk Deviation Index (BRDI), which integrates temporal irregularity, behavioral entropy, transaction velocity, burst activity, and historical behavioral drift into a unified behavioral state representation. BRDI adaptively regulates the fusion of Isolation Forest-based statistical anomaly scores and reconstruction-based nonlinear anomaly scores according to each employee’s behavioral profile. The framework further combines calibrated ensemble risk scoring, SHAP-based explainability, and blockchain-assisted audit verification using SHA-256 hashing and Merkle-root validation. Experimental evaluation on 52,846 anonymized salary advance transactions demonstrates that the framework supports behavior-aware anomaly detection, interpretable risk prioritization, and trustworthy audit traceability in enterprise financial environments. The proposed approach contributes a unified behavioral state representation, a deterministic adaptive anomaly fusion mechanism, and an integrated architecture for trustworthy AI-assisted salary advance monitoring.
